News.title: Council house where Ann Widdecombe’s ‘killer’ lived is sealed up with steel shutters after man, 28, charged with murder
News.content:
SEALED UP Council house where Ann Widdecombe’s ‘killer’ lived is sealed up with steel shutters after man, 28, charged with murder

THE council house home of Ann Widdecombe’s alleged killer has been sealed up with steel shutters.

Joshua Kerry, 28, was arrested at the red-brick terraced property in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, four days after the veteran politician was murdered.



The 78-year-old was struck over the head 21 times with a hammer at her remote home on July 8, a court was told.

A kitchen camera is said to have caught the alleged killer entering her Dartmoor bungalow as the Reform spokeswoman ate lunch.



He is believed to have been inside for just two minutes before driving off.

Separate CCTV footage obtained by The Sun showed Kerry leaving his home on the morning of the murder and returning later that night.

Ring doorbell footage also captured the moment cops pounced on their prime suspect.

His home was forensically searched and his red Vauxhall Corsa seized.



Kerry was arrested on suspicion of murder and then further arrested for the alleged “commission, preparation and instigation” of a terrorist act.

The doors and windows of his former home were this week covered by steel shutters.

He has not been charged under terrorist legislation, but police say investigations continue to try to establish whether the motive was political.

Kerry has since appeared at the Old Bailey charged with Strictly star Ann’s murder.

He was arrested 300 miles away from Widdecombe’s home when cops stormed his property.



It was confirmed to the court that an investigation into terrorist offences is ongoing, but no definite position had been reached.

During Kerry’s court appearances the court heard Ann had been eating her lunch when a man arrived at her property in a red Vauxhall Corsa.

He allegedly walked in through an open front door and asked Ann: “Don’t suppose you have bank cards and ID?”

The former MP was then hit 21 times with a hammer over the head before being tipped from her chair on to the floor, it was said.



Ann’s wallet was removed from her handbag and the suspect left just two minutes later, the court heard.

Ann had carried out two media interviews that morning and was due to appear in an online chat with C5’s Matt Allwright at 12.50pm that day, it was said.

Kerry appeared emotionless in the dock as he was flanked by two plain clothed police officers and single security guard.

He spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address during the hearing.



At the Old Bailey it was heard Kerry allegedly hit Ann in a “planned and targeted” attack carried out with a “ferocity of violence.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The defendant was then remanded into custody ahead of a hearing on October 9.

He was driven away from court by counter-terror cops in a three-car escort of a Mercedes, Land Rover Defender and Kia.

News.title: Map reveals UK’s worst stalking and harassment hotspots – as offences soar with thousands more attacks in the last year
News.content:
STALKER SURGE Map reveals UK’s worst stalking and harassment hotspots – as offences soar with thousands more attacks in the last year

THE UK’s worst stalking and harassment hotspots have been revealed as numbers continue to soar, according to new statistics.

Shocking new figures show 623,574 incidents of stalking and harassment recorded in England and Wales in the year to March 2026 – a 4 per cent rise, or 24,526, compared to the previous year.

But there’s one area that has emerged as the country’s worst with a rate of 18.7 stalking and harassment offences per 1,000 people – soaring above the national average of 10.1.



West Yorkshire Police, the fourth largest police force in the UK, recorded the highest rate of stalking and harassment cases per head, according to Home Office data.



The force covers five areas in the county – Bradford, Calderdale, Kirklees, Leeds, and Wakefield – and also ranked as the second worst area for sexual offences.

Remarkably, the figure of 10,639 offences is one percentage point down on the previous year.

Overall, police recorded stalking and harassment increased by 4 per cent to 623,574 offences.



The ONS say this is because of a 6 per cent rise in stalking to 143,704 offences and a 6 per cent rise in harassment – including racially or religiously aggravated harassment – to 320,914 offences.

And the area to see the biggest increase over the last twelve months was Devon and Cornwall which saw an astonishing 32 per cent surge.



There was also a 14 per cent rise recorded in London, a 13 per cent rise in Essex and a 12 per cent rise in Hertfordshire.

Meanwhile, British Transport Police recorded a horrifying 34 per cent rise in stalking and harassment across railways in England and Wales.

The second worst area for stalking and harassment offences recorded by police is Avon and Somerset where 15.0 offences were recorded per 1,000 people.

It is closely followed by Humberside (14.6), Greater Manchester (14.4), Cleveland (14.0) and Gwent (13.9).

London still places below the national average with a rate of 7.0 stalking and harassment offences per 1,000 despite the percentage increase.



In October last year, Samuel Hunter, 33, was jailed for bombarding a woman with unwanted messages, tracking her car and assaulting her.

He was sentenced at Leeds Crown Court after he admitted a series of offences against the woman in addition to stalking offences against another woman and a man.

During a period of between September and December 2024, he emailed her 95 times and rang 130 times.



Elsewhere, a “cruel” man who traumatised four women was sentenced to 12 months behind bars for stalking in Bristol.

Piersaverio Finizio, aged 30, approached four women who were on their own.

Police said on one occassion he told a victim three times “you look lonely, I want to be your valentine” before he followed her as she fled.

In another incident, he told a woman he would accompany her to where she was going before saying “you will be an angel soon” and asking for her phone number several times.

One victim said in a statement read out at court: “Since it happened, I haven’t known peace. I’m anxious all the time. I flinch at footsteps or when someone walks too close. I scan faces in crowds, always expecting to see him again.



Full list of areas ranked by stalking and harassment offences Stalking and harassment offences per 1,000 people in year to March 2026 West Yorkshire 18.7 Avon and Somerset 15.0 Humebrside 14.6 Greater Manchester 14.4 Cleveland 14.0 Gwent 13.9 Staffordshire 13.7 South Yorkshire 13.5 Derbyshire 12.9 North Wales 12.3 South Wales 11.9 Dyfed-Powys 11.7 Durham 11.7 Cheshire 11.6 West Midlands 11.4 Merseyside 11.3 Lancashire 10.8 Northumbria 10.4 Devon and Cornwall 10.4 Hampshire 10.2 Cumbria 10.1 Kent 9.8 Gloucestershire 9.7 Essex 9.7 Northamptonshire 9.4 Leicestershire 9.2 Hertfordshire 9.0 West Mercia 8.6 Lincolnshire 8.5 Nottinghamshire 8.5 Cambridgeshire 7.6 Thames Valley 7.5 Bedfordshire 7.0 Metropolitan Police 7.0 Dorset 6.9 Warwickshire 6.7 Surrey 6.6 Sussex 6.5 Norfolk 6.1 Wiltshire 5.8 North Yorkshire 5.3 Suffolk 4.8

“That first time, he said, ‘it must be scary being a girl at night’. That sentence broke something in me. It wasn’t just cruel, it was deliberate. He knew what he was doing.”

The police force area with the lowest number of stalking and harassment offences was Suffolk (4.8 per 1,000), followed by North Yorkshire (5.3).

In the year to March 2026, of people aged 16 and above, the ONS said around 4.9million people had experienced some form of harassment, including one-off incidents.

That marks a 8.3 per cent increase compared to incidents in the year to March 2025.

They added that an estimated 1.1million people experienced repeated harassment in the last year.



Earlier this year, the Government published its Crime and Policing Act 2026 which makes it easier for Stalking Protection Orders (SPOs) to be made.

SPOs were introduced in 2020 to restrict the activities of suspected offenders without the need for them to be convicted first – breaching one can result in five years in prison, an unlimited fine or both.

And in March, the CPS launched its first Stalking Action Plan to help prosecutors “tackle the offence in the digital age”.

On National Striking Awareness Week in April, Professor Clive Ruggles, father of Alice Ruggles and Chair of Alice Ruggles Trust said: “Ten years ago, my daughter Alice was stalked relentlessly by an ex-boyfriend after she ended their relationship.

“Over the next three months, the stalking rapidly escalated. He then broke into her flat and killed her. Could her death have been prevented if the right measures had been taken during those three months? I absolutely believe so.



“This keeps happening and we need to stop it. We urgently need practitioners across criminal justice and beyond to better understand the risks of stalking and the very real danger of escalation all the way to homicide.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Emma Lingley-Clark, Interim Chief Executive Officer of the Suzy Lamplugh Trust added: “If the Government is serious about its commitment to halve violence against women and girls it must mandate specialist independent training for criminal justice professionals working on stalking cases and ensure that stalking is included in the ‘Steps to Safety’ training programme for healthcare professionals.

“Failure to do so will continue to cost lives.”

News.title: Conman who used Pablo Escobar’s name and half-naked models to sell fake gold phones & flamethrowers jailed for 4 years
News.content:
A CONMAN who used Pablo Escobar’s name to sell non-existent gold phones and flamethrowers to fans of the infamous drug lord has been jailed.

Head of Escobar Inc, Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, used half-naked models to market products he claimed were linked to the cartel kingpin.



Tacky ads showed scantily-clad women flaunting the branded phones and posing with the “Escobar Flamethrower”.

In a bid to drum up public demand Gustafsson sent foil-wrapped Samsung Galaxy flip phones to tech reviewers.



But some suspicious recipients quickly noticed red flags.

YouTuber Marques Brownlee slammed the scam in a video posted in July 2024.

“Those people were getting scammed out of their money,” he said.

“Honestly, in hindsight, I don’t know how they thought they were gonna get away with this.”



Brownlee said the FBI turned up and asked him for the phone and any communication he had with the company.

Officials said the products, outside of the promotional spots, never existed.

Gustafsson had used a copy of Elon Musk’s “Not a Flamethrower” products and the duped mobiles for advertising.

Keen fans looking for a piece of Escobar’s legacy paid via PayPal, Stripe, Coinbase, and direct wire transfers, but the items never arrived.

Meanwhile conman Gustafsson raked in a $1.3million fortune.



When paying customers demanded refunds, the fraudster mailed them promotional books.

He then showed the proof of those mailings to payment processors to falsely claim the orders had been completed.

Proceeds were laundered across international funnel accounts in the United States, Sweden, and the United Arab Emirates.



Gustafsson was sentenced to four years in jail at a Los Angeles court on Friday.

He was also ordered to give back the $1.3million proceeds of his fraud schemes and fined an additional $25,000.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Spain extradited Gustafsson in 2023 back to the US, and he has been in federal custody since March 2025.

He previously pleaded guilty in July 2025 to a myriad of fraud and money-laundering charges.

News.title: I’m hunting the Brit ‘sex tourists’ who fathered babies like Theo – UK men could get a knock on the door
News.content:
BABY Theo Raymundo doesn’t cry. His family say he rarely does.

“He’s such a good baby,” coos his aunt, Sharan, 41. “He almost never makes a sound.”



Even when Theo’s mouth is prised open to collect DNA from inside his tiny cheek, he barely makes a noise.

It’s a simple swab test that could change his life beyond recognition.



Four-month-old Theo is one of the 100s of forgotten children born to women – including sex workers – in the Philippines and then allegedly abandoned by their British fathers.



While these British holiday makers might have taken a plane home and left their responsibilities behind, advances in DNA testing and crusading charity workers mean they could now face being pursued for child support in the British courts.

If DNA tests prove the man we suspect is Theo’s dad, he can be held accountable and forced to pay for his child’s upbringing. It could lift the baby from poverty so extreme that there’s barely enough money for food, let alone for school pencils or medical care.

I am the head of a charity that helps track down the fathers who have left their children behind.

We believe Theo’s father is a wealthy British businessman now living the high life in Dubai. The man’s life on social media is a flashy photobook of expensive cocktails, nights out and fancy cars.



In stark contrast, Theo, whose mother Liezel died in childbirth last year, lives in a crowded concrete shack in Angeles City, about 85km north-east of Manila.

Sadly – as The Sun’s exclusive new investigation series Looking for Dad: The Children of Britain’s Sex Tourists reveals – he is not alone in his plight.

Around 180,000 Brits visit the Philippines each year, and in Angeles, you rarely see a Western woman alone, but there are plenty of men. This is where boys come to play.

The city is at the centre of the Southeast Asian sex tourism industry, boosted by the existence of a former US airbase three miles away.

Women who fall pregnant to foreign visitors are often left high and dry as fathers deny their children, block contact and refuse financial support. Other men simply have no idea they’ve become a dad.



I first came to Angeles City as a journalist ten years ago, and began to write about the children of foreign fathers who live here – and the lives of their mothers.

The stories I wrote drew attention, and I founded a charity, Angeles Relief Inc, based in my home country of Australia.

As a charity, we raise money to provide welfare support to the abandoned children of foreign fathers in the Philippines.



We pay for decent accommodation, food, medical costs and school supplies – trying to keep the kids in school to give them a chance of options in the future.

There are lots of reasons to visit the Philippines, but in Angeles City, there is really only one attraction.

There are Facebook groups and dedicated websites that cater to the men who visit: Angeles City, they say, is a place where “you can’t help but get laid”.

Men often boast that they don’t use condoms, with one writing: “I took an unopened box of 40, and came home with an unopened box.”

Even if the women object, they tell me the men often ignore their pleas.



Prostitution here is illegal, but it is a bit like saying it never rains in London.

The euphemism is to be a “bar girl”, or a dancer, or a waitress. Desperate poverty means the boundaries between dating and prostitution, between being a bar girl and a sex worker, are blurry.

The family of Theo’s mum, Liezel, told me she was never a sex worker but met the man she claims is her son’s father when she worked at one of the bars sex tourists frequent.

They claimed Theo’s ‘father’ had been there several times.

Her family told me when the man visited Angeles City again in March last year, he got in touch with Liezel on WhatsApp, asking her to organise his room bookings – and a cold beer for his arrival.



I have seen messages that were allegedly shared between Liezel and the dad.

In one, she writes that she is worried because she was fertile when they had sex.

He advised her to take the morning-after pill, which she did, but she later claimed it was too late.

In another message, Liezel tells the man she is pregnant, and he replies: “Is it mine?”

The messages also reveal talk of an abortion, but Liezel went ahead with her pregnancy. Abortion is illegal in the Philippines – and always a risky procedure.



The family say the pregnancy had complications, and Liezel was so sick that she lost her job and had to sell her possessions and move in with her sisters. We have seen a message she sent in June in which she asks the British man for help with her medical bills.

The reply she received reads: “I told you I didn’t want the kid you said you was going to get rid of it and you have kept it not my fault that was your choice take care.”

Liezel died in childbirth in November last year after her blood pressure dropped and she was rushed to hospital with catastrophic bleeding.



Since then, the man we suspect is Theo’s father has been contacted by her friends and family. In messages, he was shocked to hear of her death, but says he doesn’t believe the child is his.

He did not respond to our requests to do a DNA test to establish the matter.

But I am onto him. Theo’s DNA sample is currently being analysed. Within a few weeks, we will have the results. And then we will hopefully be contacting the man.

As an organisation, we started doing something radical in 2020 to track down the fathers of the Filipino children left behind.

We utilise vast private databases that people sign up to in an effort to find family, matching DNA to abandoned Filipino children.



So far, we have successfully taken men to court in Canada, New Zealand, Australia and the US – now we begin in the United Kingdom. The laws are there to help us.

If a person uploads their DNA to a database, it is often possible to trace their family connections or a distant relative – a third or second cousin, for example.

We started using DNA sampling and genealogical detective work to trace the fathers, aided by a small team of forensic genealogists and a lot of volunteer effort.



Then comes the hard bit. We contact the men.

Sometimes they don’t know they have a child. Sometimes they knew all too well, but escaped responsibility simply by leaving the country and blocking the mother.

I’d love to say that they all take responsibility and do some version of the right thing. That is true in only about a third of cases.

More often, they block us, deny us and avoid us.

It was summed up to me most crudely in the words of one British man I contacted: “She was a hooker, for f***s sake.”



The child, he said, was therefore nothing to do with him.

Sometimes we have to take legal action – which we do with the help of a growing international network of lawyers who act for the children and their mothers without charge.

If it is proved the British businessman is Theo’s father, it would have a profound impact on his upbringing.

His aunt, Grace Raymundo, works overseas in a factory job in Korea, having left her own 14-year-old daughter to be cared for by her parents and sisters, so that the children, including Theo, at least have enough to eat.

Grace sends all she can – about 40,000 pesos a month, or about just over £500, to support six people – Theo, his older sister, Grace’s own child and her parents and sister.



It’s not only British men who deny their offspring.

Walking through the streets of the slums in Angeles City, you can see a United Nations of faces – children who clearly have foreign fathers. Europeans, Americans, African Americans, Chinese and Koreans.

THE LAW By Margaret Simons Supporting your children is not only a moral responsibility, but also a legal one in almost all countries of the world, including the Philippines and the United Kingdom. Coming to a sensible and amicable agreement between mothers and fathers is usually in everyone’s best interests. But as a last resort, we find lawyers to act for the children and their mothers and go to court. The United Kingdom and the Philippines have a reciprocal enforcement maintenance order arrangement. This means the British authorities and courts will enforce a

legitimate child support application from a Philippines-based parent.

The legal obligation to support your children does not depend on whether the mother and father were married, or had a long-term relationship. If the father is not acknowledged on the birth certificate, then its more complicated and a special application with additional evidence, such as a DNA test, will have to be made. If the father won’t provide DNA evidence, then an application can be made to the courts to make a declaration of parentage on the basis of any other evidence provided, and taking into account the father’s refusal. The courts can also order a father to do a DNA test if they decide it is in the child’s best interests. If the British authorities decide a father is due to pay child support, then they use a formula based on the income of both parents to decide the amount. Failure to pay child support can lead to money being deducted direct from wages or pensions, or bailiffs can be sent to collect on the debt. We have succeeded in helping mothers to take the legal path in Canada, New Zealand, Australia and the USA – now we begin in the United Kingdom – the laws are there. If a child was born on or after 1 July 2006 to a Filipino mother and a British citizen, then they are automatically British citizens. They can apply to the British Government for a letter to confirm this, and then for a British passport – but would have to provide evidence of parentage. Again, the courts can be asked to order a DNA test.

Britain and the Philippines are both signatories to an international treaty that would see children like Theo eligible for British citizenship and support from the men who disowned them.

In practice, the barriers for a poor family with inadequate English and no money are insurmountable unless the father cooperates.



However, getting the Philippine government to forward an application to Britain can take up to 18 months, in our experience, and the families have no money for lawyers to take the matter to court and force the father to do a DNA test.

There are no official estimates, and no way of knowing for sure how many children of British sex tourists there are here. In the chaos of the slums, many of the kids lack birth certificates.

They barely exist to their own government, let alone to Britain.

Out of sight of the tourists, concrete block shanties and shed-like homes built of the refuse from building sites tumble down to nameless creeks littered with plastic. These streams are often both the source of drinking water and the toilet.

Many homes – sometimes little more than sheds and shacks – lack running water or sanitation.



The laneways of the slums are often too narrow for any vehicle except a motorbike.

For women raised in poverty, often not even finishing school, there are few alternatives to sex work. Unemployment in the Philippines is high, and even working in a fast food restaurant requires school completion, if not a college degree.

When the women get too old, or when a relationship with a foreign man collapses, many become rubbish pickers combing the dumps on the edge of the slums for discarded food and materials they can sell.

When the young women arrive at work in the main red light district of Fields Avenue, they shed their workday shorts and T-shirts, the identity of mother, and brush their hair till it shines, don their skimpy costumes and prepare to meet the tourists, laugh at their jokes, and tell them they are hot.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the reality is that, should they get pregnant, their babies will be abandoned and the women forced to face the music alone.



Coming next in our Looking for Dad series: Chasing the Birmingham father who left a five-year-old daughter in the Angeles slums.

News.title: Fresh CCTV released in frantic search for girl, 16, who vanished nearly a month ago
News.content:
FIND HER Fresh CCTV released in frantic search for girl, 16, who vanished nearly a month ago

FRESH CCTV images have been released in a desperate search for a girl who went missing nearly a month ago.

Jessica, 16, from Tameside, was last seen 17 days ago after travelling to Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester.



Cops previously thought Jessica had been seen at Granada Park, in Denton, at 7.15pm that evening.

But in a major update officers have now know Jessica was travelling to Manchester’s city centre as she was spotted getting off a bus at Piccadilly Gardens at 8.25pm.



She had boarded the bus from the Windsor Road area of Denton, police said.

The new CCTV images show Jessica on a bus and carrying two bags, wearing a black zip-up top and sandals.

Police previously disclosed that Jessica had no access to a phone or money.

She has been classed as a “high-risk” missing person, with multiple appeals to find her issued in recent days.

Anyone with information that could help police find Jessica is urged to come forward as soon as possible.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “We are desperately doing everything we can to locate Jessica who has been missing from Tameside since Thursday, July 16 2026.



“She was last seen getting off a bus at Piccadilly Gardens at around 8.25pm, having travelled from the Windsor Road area of Denton.

“We and her family are incredibly concerned about her and want to make sure she is safe and well.”

Cops have urged the public to keep their eyes peeled for Jessica and to share any information they may have on her whereabouts.

You can contact the police on 0161 856 9325 quoting reference number MSP/06GG/0001262/26.

The force have also launched a public portal for people to share any CCTV, mobile phone or dashcam footage of the missing teen.



GMP said: “We hope that we can gather as much information as we can which will help us locate Jessica and bring her home safely.”

News.title: ‘People smugglers’ arrested as Moroccan migrants caught trying to enter Spain on jet ski after 60k breached Ceuta border
News.content:
SUSPECTED people smugglers have been arrested after trying to sneak Moroccan migrants into mainland Spain on jet skis and speedboats.

Cops believe the migrants likely entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco alongside 60,000 others earlier in the week before attempting to dash across the Strait of Gibraltar.



One of the alleged criminals was stopped by cops while piloting a speedboat across the 11-mile stretch of water from Ceuta into Spain with 11 Moroccan nationals on board.

The Spanish Civil Guard intercepted the journey and seized the speedboat, towing it back to port in Ceuta, which sits at the top of North Africa.



The captain of the motorboat is under the age of 18, according to local residents.

The nationalities of the two suspects have not been made public and it is not clear if they are in jail or have been released on bail.



Making the journey between Ceuta and Spain on a jet ski takes between 30 and 45 minutes.

Gangs typically charge nearly £3,500 a head to smuggle a migrant from Ceuta into Spain, say cops.

It comes after 60,000 migrants flooded into Ceuta – a city with a population of 84,000 – across Thursday and Friday.



Terrified locals cowered in their homes as the streets turned into open toilets in “apocalyptic” scenes.

One Spanish business owner told RTVE: “He said authorities had “no capacity” to control the chaos and that migrants are now bathing in public fountains and sleeping in the streets.

“It’s like an apocalypse. Waves of people everywhere.”

At least 72 people were killed in the surge, many drowning.



Others were crushed to death in a terrifying stampede near a beach border crossing.

Thousands of children are thought to among the huge crowds.

Most swam around the border from Morocco after seeing social media posts claiming they would be offered Spanish citizenship if they made it to Ceuta.

Other migrants clung to the backs of trucks as they breached the borders of the Spanish enclave.



The Spanish government unleashed soldiers to take back control of the city as other European nations clamp down on borders.

France has tightened its borders in response to the deepening crisis and Italy has suspended EU Schengen free-travel deal with the country.

The Schengen agreement is a treaty that allows passport-free travel across 29 European countries.

But after thousands of migrants “completely invaded” Ceuta – an enclave in northern Africa – concerned governments are rallying to remove Spain.



The surge has also sparked fears of a wave of illegal migration into the UK.

Shadow Foreign Secretary Priti Patel has claimed some of those who made it into Ceuta would “inevitably try to make their way to the UK.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Reform leader Nigel Farage reacted to the border crisis by warning: “Thousands of young men, lots of them dangerous, will be heading towards Calais and our country. It’s time to wake up. This is a battle for our civilization.”

More than 49,000 people have now voluntarily returned to Morocco, said Spanish officials.

News.title: Mum of Henry Nowak’s killer put in ‘female Monster Mansion’ holding Lucy Letby, Constance Marten & Sara Sharif’s stepmum
News.content:
THE vile mum of Henry Nowak’s killer Vicrum Digwa has been moved onto a “cushy” jail unit at the “female Monster Mansion” housing Lucy Letby and Constance Marten.

Kiran Kaur – jailed for hiding the knife Digwa used to stab student Henry, 18 – has been switched to notorious Unit 4 at HMP Bronzefield for her own safety.



The prison wing houses killers including ex-nurse Letby, 36, baby death aristocrat Constance Marten, 38, and Sara Sharif‘s killer stepmum Beinash Batool, 31.

Kaur, 53, was previously held on a separate block at Bronzefield, Surrey, but was switched to Unit 4 after being sentenced for assisting an offender.



The wing is “enhanced” where lags get extra privileges – meaning there is less violence as cons fear being moved if they attack anyone.

But a source said: “It stinks that Kaur has been moved there. It is one of the most comfortable wings on the prison estate and they’ve done it so she is safe.”



Unit 4 holds long-term, life-sentenced and enhanced-level prisoners and is known for having better conditions compared to other prison wings.

Inmates are said to have access to a hair and beauty salon while cells have their own showers, TVs and DVD players, reports the Daily Star.

A source told the outlet that the unit was “cushty” and claimed Kaur was sent there after she “pretended” she couldn’t speak English.

It comes as The Sun can reveal killer Digwa – who murdered Henry in Southampton and claimed he had been the victim of a racist attack – is still in a segregation unit at Frankland Prison, Durham as he fears mixing with other lags on a wing.

He is said to be “literally shaking with fear” behind bars after becoming a target for some of Britain’s most dangerous inmates.



Digwa, 23, knifed 18-year-old Henry Nowak five times in a random street attack as the teen made his way home from a night out.

The killer then filmed Henry as he tried to flee over a fence while leaving a trail of blood and shouting “I’m going to die”.

When cops arrived, Digwa accused the teen of making racist remarks – causing officers to place Henry in handcuffs as he lay dying.

Shocking video footage revealed the moment Digwa told his mother to take the knife he used to kill Henry away from the crime scene.

Taken on Digwa’s phone, which is pointed at the ground, he can be heard speaking to Kaur in Punjabi, asking her to remove the knife.



Kaur was jailed last month for three years for assisting an offender.

Digwa himself was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years on June 1 for the murder of Henry.

Sentencing Kaur, Judge William Mousley KC said the mum’s actions “added to your son’s pretence that he had done nothing wrong and that he was the victim”.



He continued: “A responsible parent would have challenged their son over their actions and encourage them to do the right thing.

“Instead you took the knife home and put it with a larger collection of ceremonial and other weapons in your son’s bedroom.

“That would have helped to conceal what it had been used for.”

The Sun has previously reported on how Lucy Letby and murdered Sara Sharif’s stepmother Beinash Batool had struck up a friendship in the female “Monster Mansion”.

We reported how both inmates – who have “enhanced” privileges – spend hours trying to out-manoeuvre each other into checkmate on the jail unit.



At Christmas, inmates were invited to an opera workshop with festive goodies laid on behind bars.

Letby was sentenced for the murders of seven babies and the attempted murders of seven more while a neonatal nurse at the Countess of Chester Hosptial in 2015 and 2016.

She was senteneced to 15 whole-life orders – but her case is at the centre of a high-profile miscarriage of justice campaign.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Batool was jailed in December 2024 for the horrific murder of her tortured stepdaughter.

Others on the unit included aristocrat Constance Marten, 39 – jailed over the on-the-run death of her baby daughter – and killer mum Sian Hedges, 29.

News.title: One in 10 Brits haven’t taken a bath in more than a decade, new study finds
News.content:
NOSE YOUR LIMITS One in 10 Brits haven’t taken a bath in more than a decade, new study finds

ONE in 10 Brits haven’t taken a bath in more than a decade, according to research.

A poll of 2,000 adults found 51 per cent agreed bathing has fallen out of fashion, with 20 per cent of those who don’t indulge regularly blaming a lack of time to relax.



While 33 per cent are too impatient for the time they take to run.

Other reasons for the decline in popularity included not wanting to use too much water for either cost-saving (24 per cent) or environmental (22 per cent) reasons.



But 48 per cent are just “shower people” who don’t like the idea of hanging around in a warm puddle.

The phenomenon goes beyond preference though, as 18 per cent of people don’t even have a bath in their homes.



Recent studies, such as the Shower Market Report have seen an uptick in renovations being done to remove unused baths, even if they were included in the first place – in favour of walk-in showers, wet rooms, or additional floor space.

This data is backed up by the 21 per cent who have had a tub removed from their homes in a quest to create a larger shower space (43 per cent), modernise their bathroom (42 per cent), or convert to a walk-in shower (31 per cent).

Others (14 per cent) made this renovation specifically to help reduce their water usage.

A spokesperson from leading smart Pay-As-You-Go energy supplier Utilita, which commissioned the research to support its award winning High5 tips series , including to keep showers to four minutes maximum, said: “Once a staple of the home, baths seem to have fallen out of favour for many across the UK.



“From homes getting smaller to costs getting higher, there are numerous reasons why this might be.

“But however you choose to clean and refresh, the most important thing is being conscious about your water usage, for the sake of both your pocket and the planet.”

While bathing is clearly on the outs, 30 per cent went so far as to say it will become completely extinct within the next 10 years.

Reasons for baths falling out of fashion range from busier lifestyles (55 per cent) and smaller homes (53 per cent) to rising costs of both energy (55 per cent) and water (70 per cent).

Higher prices likely also form part of the reason 77 per cent describe themselves as conscious of the amount of water they use.



Nine in 10 (90 per cent) also take active steps to reduce their consumption, such as only filling the kettle with the water they need (55 per cent), collecting rain to water plants (29 per cent), limiting hosepipe use (29 per cent), and re-using grey water (13 per cent).

More than a third (35 per cent) have also swapped baths for showers for this precise reason, according to the OnePoll.com data.

Three quarters (76 per cent) also believe this makes a difference to reducing their water bills, with 77 per cent saying the same about taking shorter showers.

The average shower now lasts for nine minutes, but when asked what could be done to reduce this even further, costs were the key motivator.

Three in 10 (32 per cent) said knowing exactly how much money they could save or seeing real-time costs per minute (30 per cent) would convince them to cut down.



Utilita’s spokesperson added: “Swapping baths for showers or reducing the time spent doing either can be a small, easy change that can have a lasting impact.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s great to see so many people are already doing this and have faith in the money they could save on their bills from this simple act.

“And no matter whether you prefer baths or showers, everyone can be a water-savvy person.”

News.title: Premium Bond 'delay' alert as customers given new date to claim big money wins
News.content:
Premium Bond 'delay' alert as customers given new date to claim big money wins

Millions of Premium Bond customers are being forced to wait just that little bit longer to see if they have won £1 million

View 2 Images The August draw is expected to see more than 6.4 million prizes paid out

August is finally here, but Premium Bond holders will notice something has changed. Millions of customers must now wait a little longer to find out whether they have landed a huge prize after NS&I issued a new update.

‌



Normally, Premium Bond draws take place at the start of each month. However, because August 1 falls on a weekend this year, the August 2026 draw will instead be held on Monday, August 3.

‌



That means the two £1 million jackpot winners will learn of their life-changing windfall on Monday. The remaining prize winners will be able to check whether they've won from Tuesday, August 4, when NS&I updates its online Prize Checker and app.

‌



The August draw is expected to see more than 6.4 million prizes paid out, with a total prize fund of around £447 million. Alongside the two millionaire prizes, there will also be awards worth £100,000, £50,000, £25,000 and thousands of smaller tax-free prizes down to £25.

Customers who have registered for notifications may receive an email or text from NS&I if they have won. Those alerts do not reveal the prize amount, meaning savers will still need to use the Prize Checker to find out how much they've received.

‌



The quickest way to check is through the official NS&I Prize Checker, which is available online and through the Premium Bonds app. According to NS&I, the checker also displays prizes won in the previous six draws, along with any older unclaimed prizes linked to your holder's number.

View 2 Images NS&I has announced key changes to the Premium Bonds scheme (Image: Getty)

Anyone hoping to take part in future draws should remember that newly purchased Premium Bonds are not entered immediately. NS&I says bonds must be held for one full calendar month before they become eligible for a prize draw.

Article continues below

The delay may leave savers waiting an extra couple of days, but it will not affect their chances of winning. Premium Bonds continue to offer tax-free prizes backed by HM Treasury, with savers able to hold up to £50,000 worth of bonds.

Even if you don't receive a notification this month, it could still be worth checking your account. NS&I says there is no time limit to claim a Premium Bonds prize, with thousands of winning prizes remaining unclaimed because customers have moved house or failed to update their contact details.

News.title: Met Office confirms July is driest on record as heatwaves plunge UK into drought
News.content:
Met Office confirms July is driest on record as heatwaves plunge UK into drought

Half of England and all of Wales are now in drought after what is set to be their driest July on record as the country has seen extreme temperatures this year

View 3 Images A view of a very dry Primrose Hill in London (Image: Akira Suemori/Shutterstock)

England and Wales are set to have seen their driest July since records began with drought affecting much of the country following extreme temperatures.

‌



Half of England is in drought says the Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales revealed all its areas are similarly, which is the third time it has happened over the past five years

‌



Fields and lawns have turned brown with the UK having had four heatwaves since May which has fuelled wildfires, with the conditions described by the Met Office as "remarkable".

‌



July has been characterised by an “exceptional combination of extreme heat, abundant sunshine and an almost complete absence of rainfall”, the forecaster said.

View 3 Images An aerial view of Richmond Park in London (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

Met Office names 29 areas facing heavy rain on Monday – see full list READ MORE :

Provisional statistics show that only 5.6mm of rainfall has been recorded in England in July so far, which is less than half of the previous record of 13.4mm set in 1911.

‌



Meanwhile, Wales is also tracking its driest July with 7.9mm of rainfall recorded, almost a third of the previous record of 22.6mm set in 1911. Northern Ireland is on track for its eighth driest July while the UK as a whole is on course for its third driest. Scotland has received 72% of its average rainfall for the month and is not currently within its top 10 driest Julys.

The figures were released with one day of July still remaining but the Met Office said the emerging picture is “one of a truly exceptional July”. It said: “A prolonged heatwave, exceptionally low rainfall and widespread drought conditions have combined to make July 2026 a remarkable month.”

Met Office Scientist Dr Emily Carlisle said: “The headline story for July is undoubtedly the rainfall. Across parts of England and Wales we’ve seen extraordinarily low totals, with some locations recording little or no meaningful rainfall for much of the month.

‌



“Provisional figures suggest this could be one of the driest Julys in nearly two centuries of records, which is particularly notable when coupled with the exceptional heat experienced so far this summer.”

View 3 Images Firefighters tackling a wildfire at Dunwich Heath (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

Water companies are not currently expecting a threat to drinking water supplies, as record winter rainfall means reservoirs are still close to expected levels, but more than 23 million people across England and Wales are facing hosepipe bans.

‌



Aerial pictures show the parched London landscape after weeks of hot weather and dry conditions. Much of the grass in the gardens of Buckingham Palace and Kensington Palace appears to have turned brown while only the track at Ascot Racecourse appears to look nourished.

Scorching temperatures as high as 35.2C were recorded on Wednesday, marking the seventh day in 2026 when temperatures have hit 35C or higher.

Fire chiefs said that wildfires are becoming a “recurring and growing feature of the risks facing our communities” in the face of a changing climate.

‌



Firefighters responded to 393 wildfires across England and Wales in July, making it the busiest month on record. The number of wildfire incidents recorded this year already matches the total annual figures seen in 2021, 2023 and 2024 combined, although the number is below the same point in 2025 when long-lasting drought and heat caused severe fire risk.

Firefighters have been tackling a blaze at Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, Suffolk, since 5.30pm on Wednesday. The wildfire is a few miles away from nuclear power station Sizewell B and the construction site for new power station Sizewell C.

The National Trust, which has had wildfires at a number of its sites including at Dunwich Heath, is demanding action to help people adapt to the changing climate. These demands include building homes fit for the future, creating wetter and more resilient landscapes, cooling towns and cities and helping communities.

Article continues below

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said it “is likely that 2026 could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record”, surpassing the number seen in 2022 when the UKHSA started studying them.

There have been almost double the number of excess deaths caused by heatwaves so far this year than all of last summer, the data shows. The new report estimates there were 2,877 heat-associated deaths during the heatwaves in May and June this year, with an estimated 753 deaths associated with the heatwave from May 24-27, and a further 2,124 with the heatwave between June 21 and 28.

News.title: Panic as 4.1 earthquake rocks Spanish holiday hotspot popular with Brits
News.content:
Panic as 4.1 earthquake rocks Spanish holiday hotspot popular with Brits

A 4.1 magnitude earthquake has hit southern Spain with its epicentre in Murcia and it has rocked popular tourist spots for Brits including Benidorm and Alicante

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A popular holiday destination for Brits in Spain has been rocked by a 4.1 magnitude earthquake.

‌



Emergency services have been flooded with calls following the earthquake in Murcia today which was recorded by the National Geographic Institute (IGN) at 11.59am and it is understood to have lasted for several seconds.

‌



The earthquake comes after Naples, Italy, was struck by a major 4.7 magnitude tremor that damaged buildings, cars and saw around 20 people injured on Friday.

‌



Today's earthquake in Spain reportedly rocked neighbouring areas Alicante, a popular holiday destination for Brits who also head to nearby Benidorm, and Albacete.

View 2 Images The epicentre of the earthquake in southern Spain

The quake was centred in the town of Librilla at a depth of around 3 miles with Murcia located about 18 miles away.

‌



Emergency services 112 wrote on X: The 112 Emergency Coordination Centre for the Region of Murcia has received more than 80 calls (...) at various points in the region. So far, no personal or material damage has been reported."

Spain's National Graphic Institute (IGN) says that there have been seven tremors in the past few days before this earthquake, and the increased seismic activity has led to 21 over the past month. But this is the strongest earthquake int he past six months, surpassing that on June 3 which had a magnitude of 2.3.

In 2011 Spain suffered its worst earthquake in decades which left 10 people dead in the southern Spanish town of Lorca. Hundreds of people had to be evacuated from their homes following the 5.2 magnitude tremor which saw several buildings collapse in the town which is southwest of Alicante.

Article continues below

Lines of cars lay crushed under tonnes of rubble and a hospital was also evacuated.

Southern Spain is at a higher risk from earthquakes as specifically Andalusia and Murcia are on the northern margin of collision zone between the Eurasian plate and the Nubian (African) plate, which is converging northward into Eurasia at approximately 4–5 mm/year.

This convergence which built the Atlas Mountains of Morocco and the Alps of central Europe in previous geological periods, is currently seen in southern Spain through the fault systems of the Betic Cordillera: the mountain belt running from the Gibraltar Arc in the west through Malaga, Granada, Almeria, and Murcia to the Mediterranean coast.

News.title: Great white shark weighing 100 STONE spotted off Florida tourist beach showing unusual behaviour
News.content:
Great white shark weighing 100 STONE spotted off Florida tourist beach showing unusual behaviour

A huge great white shark was spotted off the coast of a popular Florida beach but scientists revealed this predator has gone against the grain, surprising them with his behaviour

View 2 Images A 1,400lbs great white shark nicknamed Breton was near a popular Florida beach (Image: Ocearch / SWNS)

A massive 13ft long great white shark weighing a whopping 100st was unexpectedly spotted off the coast of Florida, near a popular beach, as the predator surprised scientists with its behaviour.

‌



The 1,400lbs (100st) creature, nicknamed Breton, has been heading south this summer despite other sharks swimming north for cooler waters and more food. Each summer, great whites usually follow the same pattern and travel from the Gulf of Mexico and along Florida's coast to migrate up the Atlantic towards Canada - but Breton's movements have been a complete break from the rest of the pack.

‌



On July 25 the apex predator was tracked "paving his own path down south" and his tracker "pinged" near the popular tourist spot of Daytona Beach.

‌



Pregnant woman saved from shark attack by hero fiancée as he is rushed to hospital READ MORE :

View 2 Images Breton being examined by scientists (Image: Ocearch / SWNS)

The shark's tracker, which was being monitored by OCEARCH, transmitted a locating "ping" signal when his dorsal fins is exposed above the water's surface for long enough. John Tyminki, a data scientist at the non-profit, revealed that seasonal food sources and cooler water temperatures are part of why sharks migrate north during the summer.

He added that this was not the first time this particular shark has shocked scientists. Tyminki said: "Breton always surprises us. He was tagged September 11, 2020, so it is going on nearly six years.

‌



"Our estimate is that he has travelled more than 52,000 miles. He has gone in shore and off shore and because he is a mature male he is showing us useful patterns. Right now he is off the East coast of Florida as of July 25 in the Gulf stream.

"Usually our understanding is that great white sharks at this time are in Canada or Cape Cod because of the seals and the water temperature. Yet Breton has gone somewhere different.

"We wondered, isn't the water temperature too warm for him to be there? His tag also sends us temperature data and where he is, it is on the warm side for white sharks, at 80 degrees Fahrenheit."

Article continues below

Scientists revealed they do not know why Breton has chosen to go against the grain. Tyminki added: "He is probably spending his time a lot deeper down where the water is colder. Our guess is that Breton is following seasonal schools of fish. He continues to surprise us and is amazing."

This comes after a huge shark, thought to possibly be a great white, was spotted circling a boat in Portugal on July 25. The predator was seen around two nautical miles off the coast of Nazaré - an area famous for surfing.

A video of the terrifying moment was uploaded by a boat-tour company with the caption: "This morning, between São Martinho do Porto and Nazaré, about 2MN from land, we spotted a large shark during a walk."

News.title: 'I died 3 times in Army bomb blast but I'd still let my son join up'
News.content:
Lying in the dust of Helmand Province, Lance Corporal Martyn Compton thought he was taking his last breath. His armoured vehicle had been ripped apart by a roadside IED, then rocket-propelled grenades turned it into an inferno. Engulfed in flames, as he crawled for cover, he was shot in the right leg twice, shattering his femur.

This weekend, it’s the 20th anniversary of the devastating ambush that left the Household Cavalry soldier with burns to 75 per cent of his body. Yet, as his son, Archie, approaches his 16th birthday in November - Martyn’s age when he joined-up - he says he’ll support him if he wants to become a soldier.

Martyn says: "People expect me to say I'd do everything I could to stop Archie joining the Army. That's honestly not how I feel. Of course I’d be terrified. I know exactly what can happen. I've lived through the worst. I’ve seen the true horror of war. I also know what the Army gave me. It gave me confidence, discipline, lifelong friends and opportunities I'd never have had anywhere else."

Maverick Daily Mirror hero who risked her life to entertain WWII frontline soldiers READ MORE :

Forgotten icon who changed London's Tube forever but critics wiped her name READ MORE :

View 6 Images Martyn Compton with his wife Michelle, son Archie and daughter Coral, 20 years after he was horrifically injured in Afghanistan (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

‌



He continues: “It gave me an inner self belief and resilience that gave me the fight to stay alive. For that reason, if Archie came to me tomorrow and said, 'Dad, I want to join the Army,' I'd tell him I support him. Of course I'd worry. But I'd also be incredibly proud of him."

Martyn believes too many young people are growing up without direction. He says: "We've got a generation who feel a bit lost. The defence of our nation and patriotism are dwindling, which is tough to watch when you’ve served your country. One million young people who’re not in employment, education or training.

“I worry about this generation and what the future holds for them. It’s created a nation that feels divided. There seems to be less care and respect for one another and less direction. I hope this new Government will take more steps for them. Because of this, I support National Service, including for my own children. Many countries around the world do it. Why can’t we? Some form of National Service would give you purpose. It teaches teamwork, respect and responsibility. Those lessons stay with you long after you've taken the uniform off."

‌



View 6 Images Martyn and Michelle Compton before he was injured (Image: © Press People)

On August 1, 2006, Martyn's regiment was travelling in convoy in small tanks, heading to support Danish forces in Helmand Province. The lead vehicle crossed a narrow bridge safely. As Martyn's vehicle followed, gunfire erupted. He says: "The bullets started smashing into the vehicle. As I reversed, an IED exploded and ripped our Spartan vehicle apart. Every man travelling with me lost their life. I was the sole survivor.”

Leaving him no time to think, insurgents fired rocket-propelled grenades. Martyn says: "One hit the deck. One hit the engine. Suddenly, I was completely engulfed in flames. My adrenaline kicked in. Pure instinct to survive took over. I could smell burning, but didn’t even register it was my own flesh. The pain hadn’t kicked in. My one thought was ‘I must get out of here.’”

Dragging himself from the burning vehicle, he rolled across the sand to extinguish the flames. He says: "The heat was unbelievable. I just knew I had to put the flames out." Still under heavy enemy fire, he crawled towards cover, saying: "As I reached a wall I was shot twice in my right leg.

‌



"My strongest memory isn't the pain, it was thinking, 'that's it. I'm not going home.' Then everything stopped hurting. I genuinely believed I was slipping away." He survived because fellow soldiers Andrew Radford and Mick Flynn repeatedly exposed themselves to enemy fire to reach him. Martyn, 42, of Hastings, East Sussex, says: “They did the bravest thing I've ever seen. They fought through enemy fire to get to me. They risked their own lives to save mine. "

View 6 Images Martyn and Michelle Compton on their wedding day (Image: © Press People)

In the ensuing 20 years Martyn’s had more than 500 painful skin grafts, reconstructive surgery and rehabilitation. In his most recent operation last year, surgeons operated on one of his eyes. Scars cover most of his body, but he says: "I've got used to living with them. People still stare at me sometimes in the street, or when they first meet me. I can still feel awkward and self-conscious. But my scars don't define me - my amazing family does."

Finally when home, looking unrecognisable, Martyn had a frank conversation with his then girlfriend, Michelle. He says: "I told her I'd understand if she wanted to leave.” Instead, they’ve just celebrated their 18th wedding anniversary with their children, Archie, 15, and Coral, 14, and their dog Lola, four. He says: "Michelle has been beside me through every operation, every setback and every bad day. Even in the darkest moments, there is light.This experience taught me what real love is. She's walked every step of this journey with me."

‌



Another source of support has been Prince William, who he met while he was in hospital recovering in 2007. His champion ever since, Martyn says: “Prince William was serving in my regiment when I returned injured from Afghanistan. I was still in a wheelchair when he came to see me, privately. He stopped by one day and simply said, 'If you ever need anything, let me know’. He’s been true to his word ever since.”

View 6 Images Michelle and Martyn with their dog, Lola (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

Military duties meant William couldn't attend Martyn and Michelle's wedding in July 2008, but he sent a personal message wishing them every happiness. Years later, they were invited to William's wedding to Catherine at London’s Westminster Abbey on April 29, 2011. Martyn says: "He spotted me in the Abbey straight away. Michelle and me were sat in front of the Beckhams and opposite Elton John. As Prince William walked down to take his place at the altar, we were the first ones he spoke to. He grinned and said ‘hello Compo, how are you doing?’ It was a surreal moment, to sit with all these famous people around me. That's the sort of man he is.”

Despite the decades of pain and endless operations Martyn has enjoyed some amazing experiences - including being photographed by rockstar Bryan Adams. He says: “I remember being asked to pose for Bryan, he had a converted warehouse on the Thames. Archie was just a baby and ,as we walked in ,there was a guy making a cup of tea. I didn’t think much of it and I said, ‘can I just pop in here and change Archie’s nappy? He said ‘yes of course’. Then Michelle said, ‘that’s Bryan Adams.’ His photoshoot with me ended up in the National Portrait Gallery.”

‌



Still living with PTSD, Martyn admits: "I still get nightmares. But I've learned how to cope. "Veterans' charities, especially Pilgrim Bandits, have been a lifeline. They are a small amazing charity who helped me massively and they are making a difference to the lives of injured veterans. They understand what we've all been through."

View 6 Images Martyn Compton is now fundraising to help struggling veterans (Image: © PRESS PEOPLE)

And he’s about to take on a challenge for Pilgrim Bandits, to raise money for struggling veterans. He says: “I am going to travel through the jungle of Vietnam with other injured veterans. For me, to share some camaraderie with others who have faced hell, is cathartic.” Every August 1, Martyn raises a glass to the men who never made it home. He says: "You never forget them. For most people Afghanistan is something from the past. For some of us it's still part of everyday life."

Reflecting on what an Army career would mean, should Archie choose one, he says: "The scars remind me every day what the Army took from me. But they also remind me what it gave me. So, if Archie chose that life, I'd stand beside him. Not because it would be easy. But because I’d be proud of him. Every time I look in the mirror I’m reminded of that day - but also I’m reminded of how precious life is.”

‌



To donate to Martyn’s venture for other servicemen see: www.justgiving.com/page/martyn-compton

News.title: Telling clue about Meghan and Harry's changing relationship after 'great escape'
News.content:
Telling clue about Meghan and Harry's changing relationship after 'great escape'

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle appear to be eyeing up a return to the royal fold, in some capacity. But it remains to be seen how realistic a reversal of Megxit really is

View 7 Images Harry and Meghan's star in the US is fading, experts have warned (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have a new goal. With their popularity dwindling in the US, the couple are said to be determined to mend their broken relationship with the royal family - beginning with their recent meeting with King Charles.

‌



It was the first time that the monarch had seen his grandchildren Archie and Lilibet since 2022, and Meghan's first return to Britain since the late Queen's funeral.

‌



But what is the motivation behind their renewed efforts to fix those burned bridges? Reports suggest that the couple are still pushing for a 'half-in, half-out' position within the family - something the late Queen expressly forbade.

‌



It's believed that the couple want to carry on making money to fund their lifestyle in Montecito, but also to be treated as 'working royals' when in the UK while doing charity and public speaking events.

View 7 Images The Sussexes are said to be looking for a return to the royal fold, in some capacity (Image: Netflix)

Some critics believe Harry is making his move now while he has the ear of the King - and before his older brother Prince William takes power. Certainly, there is no love lost between the siblings, and there will surely be no place for the Sussexes within the royal fold when he becomes king.

‌



Others argue the couple need their connection to the royal family in order to stay relevant. "There is definitely a feeling in his camp that he has started to feel a bit unwelcome in America," a source close to Harry told the Mail. "That has been an increasing and significant shift in sentiment, a feeling that the American dream might not be all that it was cracked up to be."

The couple's axed or reduced deals with Spotify and Netflix hint, some royal experts say, at their star fading in the States. But it's not only their American dream that has transitioned - so, too, has their relationship, according to another source.

"I don't think he's ever wanted to be estranged from his family. I think when he was madly in love with Meghan he could be blind enough to choose her," they told the publication. "Now things are different, and the veil is lifting."

‌



7 View 7 Images Sources close to the couple say their relationship has shifted into a new stage (Image: meghan/Instagram) 7 View 7 Images The couple are all loved-up on Instagram (Image: meghan /Instagram)

At the start of their romance, Harry positioned himself as Meghan's protector and defender. Most notably, he condemned the racism being directed towards her on social media in a public statement - which has since been removed from the royal family's website.

‌



He then went one step further. During the couple's now-infamous interview with Oprah Winfrey post-Megxit, they claimed that an unnamed member of the royal family expressed "concerns" about how dark their son Archie's skin might be before he was born. It caused an unprecedented crisis within the family.

Harry later denied accusing the royal family of racism during an interview with British journalist Tom Bradby ahead of the publication of his memoir Spare. But the hits kept on coming, with Harry going on to allege physical fights with William, describing a falling out between Meghan and Princess Kate, and calling Queen Camilla "the villain" and "dangerous".

View 7 Images The Sussexes reunited with King Charles earlier this month (Image: GETTY)

‌



After quitting royal life, the Sussexes were just as inseperable - embarking on joint work ventures and events to fund their new life in Montecito. Most of these projects proved to be lucrative because of their links to the royal family. But when that well dried up, they seemed to professionally separate.

Meghan launched American Riviera Orchard - now As Ever, and threw herself into her lifestyle series, With Love, Meghan, which has since been cancelled. Harry, meanwhile, focused on his charity work, though that too has proved difficult with a bitter boardroom battle at Sentebale - the charity he co-founded in honour of his late mother Princess Diana - leading to his resignation and huge heartache.

Now the couple are said to be struggling to bring any of their projects to fruition, with experts having long suggested that their connection to the royal family is what gave them real relevance.

‌



Some royal watchers have mused over whether this may have put strain on their marriage. Meghan has long been seen as the instigator - and the orchestrator - of Megxit. But sources close to Harry now say that Meghan is 'fully behind' his plans to return to the royal fold, in some capacity.

View 7 Images Meghan is reportedly 'fully behind' Harry's plans (Image: ANP/AFP via Getty Images)

The Sussexes have been married for eight years - and they have certainly gone through some major changes in that time. From being feted as a breath of fresh air for the royal family, to quitting royal life, moving to California, and becoming hugely polarising figures, they have had a rollercoaster ride. Not to mention the fact that they have become parents in that time, to Archie and Lilibet in 2019 and 2021 respectively.

‌



There's no sign of trouble in paradise from the outside, with Meghan regularly posting loved-up snaps with Harry and their children. Just last week, the Duchess shared sweet photos of the couple giggling together while on their summer holiday in Portugal.

But just like any relationship, things look different nearly a decade into marriage. Relationship expert and dating coach Hayley Quinn, tells the Mirror: "In the first flurry of love, people can often end up putting their partners on a pedestal. They can idealise their partners, and want to do anything for them. They may even attempt to show their love through overcoming adversity. In the case of Harry and Megan, Harry showed his loyalty to Megan during Megxit when the couple left their royal duties for a life in the USA.

View 7 Images The Sussexes with their children, Archie and Lilibet (Image: @meghan/Instagram)

‌



"Since then, their plans have had to survive contact with reality. This includes disappointing ratings for their podcasts and TV shows. Additionally, the couple are parents to two young children, which as every parent knows brings its own set of stresses and strains.

"It's believable that their once great escape no longer feels so gilded and the couple may be experiencing strain on their relationship. Recently there seems to be more attempts from Harry to reconnect with his family, which may suggest he's had a change of heart about the importance of his wider social relationships outside of his marriage."

Hayley continued: "Ultimately, all relationships can't survive on adrenaline and desire alone. Many formerly passionate relationships have to contend with maintaining desire after the honeymoon period has ended.

Article continues below

"Part of this work is a mental readjustment that your 'roommate years', where you are focused on coparenting, are a natural progression not a problem in your relationship. It's also totally normal to discover that your partner has some flaws, that perhaps you didn't notice in the beginning, nobody is perfect.

"The other part of the work is to find healthy outlets to keep the novelty alive and to spend quality one-to-one time together. For famous couples with demanding schedules, this may be easier said than done."

News.title: New housing development completed with help of 'Walter the robot' as UK aims to build 1.5million more homes
News.content:
New housing development completed with help of 'Walter the robot' as UK aims to build 1.5million more homes

A development built with the the help of a cutting-edge robot has just been completed. Housing chiefs say it is a ‘defining moment for the future of the construction industry’.

Andy Burnham discusses plans for new technical subjects

The race to build 1.5m new homes across the UK could be won with the help of a robot called 'Walter'.

‌



A pioneering housing development built with the help of the cutting-edge technology has just been completed. Housing chiefs say it is a ‘defining moment for the future of the construction industry’.

‌



The government aims to build 1.5m new homes in England over a five-year period, translating to an average target of about 370,00-a-year. JT Lifestyle Homes has now officially finished the development in Thornley, County Durham. It was the first in the UK to use a wall-laying terra-based robot - nicknamed WLTR or ‘Walter’ - to place bricks with speed and ultimate precision.

‌



View 3 Images A pioneering housing development has just been completed with the the help of a Robot called Walter

Miracle dog found alive after spending 29 days trapped under earthquake rubble READ MORE :

Dr Jan Telensky, founder and CEO of JT Lifestyle Homes, hopes the technology will help address the labour shortage in the construction industry. Dr Telensky said: “There is currently a severe shortage of bricklayers in the UK, along with a wider skills shortage across much of the construction industry.

"With ambitious housing targets we need to get to grips with new technology to help us meet the demand for new homes - and fast. We have been incredibly impressed with how Walter has helped us speed up build time.

‌



View 3 Images The cutting-edge Robot called Walter at work

"Using a robot which works in all weathers also meant we knew what the output would be, come rain or shine. Walter picks up and lays the bricks with precision, enhancing the overall build and literally taking the heavy lifting out of the job. It is operated by experienced trades professionals who can monitor the build and deal with the more intricate aspects of the job.”

Now finished, the Maple Close scheme boasts both cutting-edge exteriors and modern interiors. All homes are equipped with solar panels on their roofs and the homes are built with specialist clay blocks that are lower in carbon than other materials and have enhanced thermal performance.

‌



View 3 Images The Robot Walter has just completed a housing project in Co Durham (Image: JT Lifestyle Homes)

They also use less water, are lightweight and generate no mortar waste. Any damaged blocks can be crushed and reused as hardcore on site.

The UK is in the grip of a "housing crisis" and new PM Andy Burnham wants to deliver "the biggest council house building programme since the post-war period" - but has not as yet revealed any detailed plans. Keir Starmer pledged £39bn to fund the construction of 300,000 new "social and affordable houses" over the course of 10 years during the 2025 Spending Review, and said this money would "reinvigorate" council housebuilding.

Article continues below

That would equate to around 30,000 new homes a year, but the majority of those were expected to be social housing constructed by not-for-profit housing associations using government grants. Council house construction has collapsed across England since the 1980s and much of the stock of local authority homes has been sold off with the right to buy scheme of the Thatcher government.

News.title: Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades
News.content:
Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades

EXCLUSIVE: The King and Queen's principal private secretary Sir Clive Alderton is to leave his post after two decades working for the Royal Family - and thoughts have turned to his replacement

View 4 Images King Charles with his private secretary Sir Clive Alderton (Image: PA)

He has quietly been one of the most influential figures in the Royal Household for more than two decades - b ut now the King’s right-hand man, Sir Clive Alderton, is set to step down from his role next year.

This means Charles and Queen Camilla are now left with the tough task of finding a new principal private secretary. The royal aide played a pivotal role in steering the couple through Charles’ accession to the throne and has been on hand to support the King through the likes of state visits and more personal matters, earning him the nickname from Prince Harry as 'the wasp'.

King Charles pestered by troublesome fly as he and Camilla begin to wind down for summer break READ MORE :

View 4 Images The King and his right-hand man at Royal Ascot earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Whoever replaces him, when he leaves around the time of his 60th birthday next May, will become the King’s most senior courtier and the person whom he can call on for advice and act as a bridge between Crown and government. Royal expert Jennie Bond spent 14 years as the BBC’s royal correspondent, closely following the then Prince Charles and getting a glimpse into the inner workings of Buckingham Palace.

And she told the Mirror exactly what Sir Clive’s successor will need to tackle one of the demanding jobs working for the King. She explained: “I think most long-serving private secretaries become part adviser and part friend. He is someone the King will speak to almost every day of his life, someone whose principal role is to have his boss’s back, to foresee trouble and head it off before it happens.

“Like most previous private secretaries, Sir Clive is an experienced diplomat, and he played a vital role in engineering the huge success of the King’s visit to the United States earlier this year.

View 4 Images The King and Queen must now find a new private secretary (Image: Getty Images)

“Part of the job is to work closely with the Cabinet secretary and the Prime Minister’s principal private secretary and the three of them would have overseen the programme and carefully honed the witty speeches the King made.

“To Prince Harry, he was ‘the wasp’ who blocked his way and ignored his wishes. But to the King and Queen he has proved himself a safe pair of hands, and it may be that they will continue to call on his advice.

“Sir Clive is someone the King has been able to turn to, complain to, laugh with and rely on as his chief gatekeeper. His successor will indeed have big shoes to fill. Thus far they have always been men, so it would be refreshing to see a woman succeed him.”

During Sir Clive’s time as the King’s principal private secretary, he has led the monarch through his cancer diagnosis and many incoming and outgoing state visits, including his trip to Washington DC to meet US president Donald Trump, where Charles delivered an historic address to Congress.

View 4 Images Sir Clive with the King at St Paul's Cathedral (Image: Getty Images)

He has kept pace with Charles, described as a “complete workaholic” by his wife, and over the years helped turn his ideas into action. And Jennie says his replacement will need to hit the ground running. She explained: “The world is still in turmoil, the King and Queen are now elderly, with the King still undergoing treatment for cancer.

“The King‘s brother is still under police investigation, his sons are still estranged and the UK is getting to know yet another Prime Minister. The King will need someone with proven diplomatic skills, sensitivity about family matters and enough experience to deal with the shifting world of politics.”

Earlier this week, royal sources said the courtier elected to share the news that he was to step aside so that an open and rigorous recruitment process for his successor can begin, with the aim of identifying the highest calibre external and internal candidates.

The timeframe additionally allows for an appropriate period of handover to his eventual successor in spring/summer of 2027, once an appointment is made.

And Jennie added: “The Palace are going to be looking at both internal and external candidates and they have plenty of time to cast the net wide as Sir Clive will remain in post until next year.

Article continues below

“He has been at Charles’s side through some of the most critical times: the death of Queen Elizabeth, the succession and the Coronation.

“He’s reported to have come up with a very apt phrase to describe the tone of the new King’s reign: ‘informal formality’. And it does rather sum up the way Charles goes about his business – sometimes giving and receiving hugs in the way his mother never did.”

News.title: Continued drought could cause shortage of certain foods, head of farmers' union says
News.content:
There could be a shortage of certain food products if the current drought conditions continue, the National Farmers' Union (NFU) has warned.

NFU President Tom Bradshaw said yields of wheat and oats were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they have been unable to grow grass.

Drought has been declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales as successive heatwaves left water supplies under strain, with more than 20 million people now under hosepipe bans.

Amber heat health alerts have also been issued for large parts of England, including the Midlands, the South-East and the South West, until Wednesday.

News.title: Body of mountaineer Nirmal Purja recovered after Pakistan avalanche
News.content:
Prince William said he was "truly saddened to hear of the tragic death" of Purja, who he said "served with distinction" as a soldier before "becoming one of the greatest mountaineers".

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme on Saturday that her organisation feared all members of the group were dead, and that Purja had led many expeditions she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit since Thursday's avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."
