World.title: Spanish Ceuta witnesses a deadly ‘game’ for Moroccan migrants
World.content:
This weekend, thousands of Moroccans attempted to reach the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta.

For the past couple of days, I have commuted to work between Europe and Africa. When an estimated 60,000 migrants arrived in Ceuta, Spain’s autonomous outpost on the northern tip of Africa, from Morocco this week, businesses shut their doors and all available beds quickly disappeared.

So, we have been staying in the mainland Spanish port city of Algeciras, taking the one-hour ferry to and from Ceuta.

A fellow commuter is Isabel Hossein, a port police officer in Algeciras whose home is Ceuta. “I have documents, so it’s easy for me,” she says. “Sometimes I cross the border to Morocco just for lunch. Why not? The food is good.”

Isabel says the mass influx of migrants on Wednesday and Thursday was overwhelming for the residents of Ceuta. “People were afraid; there were so many young men everywhere,” she said.

“I am half Christian, half Muslim, as many in Ceuta are. We live peacefully together. But the numbers this time were scary.”

It has got me thinking about the journeys we take. At Algeciras, hundreds of cars line up daily for the ferry to Tangier. Moroccans from all over Spain, and elsewhere in Europe, depart here to go home for the summer holidays.

I am told that on motorways in Spain up to 1,000km away, the word “Algeciras” appears in Arabic to ensure people find their way here. They, of course, have documents.

In Ceuta, on Saturday, I saw hundreds of young men making their way back to Morocco on foot, under the watchful, occasionally threatening, eye of the Spanish military.

The undocumented ones

Exhausted by the heat, 48 hours earlier, the men swam to the shores of Ceuta.



“For the good life, humanity, safety, and all the things you need,” Abdelmajid said.

There was none of that available when they arrived in Ceuta, just extreme heat, thirst and a very hostile reception.

Of the estimated 60,000 Moroccans who arrived in little more than 24 hours, 90 percent had returned to Morocco by Saturday night.

Several indicated by rotating their wrists they would simply try again. “They were told to come. I saw it on Instagram, ‘Go to Spain and get money, jobs,'” she said. “It’s all a game.”

Dozens died in the attempt to reach Ceuta, and on Saturday evening, police divers were still recovering bodies from the surrounding waters.

The Spanish government blames criminal gangs and traffickers. Opposition politicians blame the left-wing Spanish government’s immigration policies for the weekend’s events, some describing it as “an invasion”.

Zia Yusuf, a senior figure in the anti-immigration Reform UK party, turned up in Ceuta to join those from the right and far right trying to set their narrative for the events.

A long way to come for a bit of social media, but this was powerful stuff: in a crisp white shirt and surrounded by muscled minders, I watched Yusuf extract a few words from young men who spoke little English.

On his X account, he told his nearly 150,000 followers: “I am in Ceuta, the scene of the 60,000 strong invasion. Spain has effectively militarised its border. Already spoken to Moroccan men here who say they are trying to get to Britain. More to come.”

No one I spoke to said they were heading for Britain. Though I’ve no doubt if you posed the question to someone with a passing idea of what you were asking – “Would you like to go to Britain?” – the answer would likely be, “yes”.

For some, it no doubt is a game. But here in Ceuta, amid the detritus of flippers and rubber floating devices that litter the beaches this weekend, a game with tragic consequences.

World.title: The Board of Peace is a failed body and should be abandoned
World.content:
The Palestinian issue should be returned to the UN framework and anchored again in international law.

On Thursday, United States President Donald Trump announced that Hamas had agreed to disarm and move to the next phase of the ceasefire deal in Gaza. The announcement was received positively by various regional actors while the US president characterised it as a “historic agreement”.

The problem is that the disarmament is unlikely to take place. That is because Hamas has made clear that it has conditioned relinquishing its weapons on Israel abiding by its obligations under the agreement, which the latter has failed to do since it was reached in October. The Board of Peace, the body tasked with overseeing the ceasefire and Gaza’s reconstruction, has done nothing to pressure it into compliance.

This is one of the many failures of this body, which has very little to show for its six-month existence. It lacks the power, financing, enforcement mechanisms and legal standing within the international legal system to fulfil its self-declared mandate. Rather than creating a pathway towards de-escalation, it has created an appearance of diplomatic progress that provides political cover for the continuation of the Israeli genocide in Gaza.

The only way to move forward is for the board to be abandoned and responsibility returned to the United Nations.

Achieving nothing

The Board of Peace was established under Article 9 of Trump’s 20-point peace plan for Gaza, announced in October. Its mandate is to oversee a temporary Palestinian technocratic body that would manage Gaza and an International Stabilization Force (ISF) of multinational peacekeepers. In theory, the board would supervise Gaza’s reconstruction and Israel’s gradual withdrawal. In practice, it has not achieved any progress on either of these processes.



Despite lofty promises from the Trump administration about transforming Gaza into a modern urban landscape, there has been no movement in that direction. The majority of the population still lives in abhorrent conditions in tents.

Last month, the board scaled down the reconstruction plan to a pilot project near Rafah, close to the Egyptian border, which is under the control of the Palestinians who collaborate with Israel. Israel would vet the Palestinians who are allowed to stay in that development.

Worse still, the board is trying to give itself the right to confiscate Palestinian properties or use them “free of charge”. This signals its willingness to serve as a facade for continuing Israeli theft of Palestinian land.

An Israeli withdrawal – the other major process the board should oversee – has been all but forgotten. Instead, Israel has continued to kill Palestinians in regular bombardments and encroach on more and more Palestinian land.

Since the ceasefire began in October, Israel has killed more than 1,100 Palestinian civilians. It has continued to carry out demolitions of Palestinian homes and to move its “Yellow Line”, expanding its control to about 70 percent of Gaza’s territory, up from 53 percent at the start of the ceasefire.

The Board of Peace has taken no action in response to these Israeli colonial practices and has not issued any public statements condemning them.

Meanwhile, the board has framed Palestinians as responsible for the lack of progress. Its high representative, Nickolay Mladenov, has described Hamas as the “principal obstacle” to implementing the ceasefire despite no recorded Palestinian attacks since its beginning.

This one-sided scrutiny reveals the board’s function: not peacemaking but providing cover for the ongoing occupation.

The Board of Peace has also maintained arrangements that allow Israel to control the flow of aid into Gaza. Although Trump’s plan stipulates that neither Hamas nor Israel should interfere with the entry and distribution of assistance, the Israeli military continues to determine both the quantity and type of assistance allowed into the Gaza Strip.

Major European countries and China have declined to join the Board of Peace. States that initially signalled a willingness to contribute to the ISF have since frozen or withdrawn their commitments.

This lack of confidence is also reflected in funding failures. Despite initial pledges of $10bn from the US and a further $7bn from other countries, the World Bank account established for the board reportedly has received no funds. Instead, it has relied on a few million dollars deposited into a private JP Morgan account, much of which has been spent on salaries and administrative overhead rather than reconstruction or civilian protection.



The return of the UN

Perhaps the starkest sign of the failure of the Board of Peace is that it is seeking to give itself immunity from prosecution. In a draft resolution, the board appears to pursue protections for its members and administrative bodies, including the Office of the High Representative, Palestinian technocrats, international military forces and nonresident contractors.

In other words, the board wants to operate above the law. The goal is clear: impose a foreign governance structure that obscures Israeli colonisation of Gaza behind an international body.

The continuing existence of such a body is an international disgrace, and it needs to end.

The appropriate response is a collective push by states that support the two-state solution and the peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict to bring the process back to the United Nations umbrella. Palestinian factions should be at the forefront of this effort.

The UN should assume responsibility and transfer any relevant functions away from the board to established UN bodies.

Critics may counter that the UN has failed to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict for more than seven decades. That is true. But its umbrella offers an international legal framework that anchors action in international law and readily identifies violations. That provides structure and legal levers the Palestinians can use to continue pushing for their rights.

What is more, there is a dedicated UN agency – UNRWA – that deals with Palestinian refugee problems and is best equipped to handle the vast challenges of a displaced and impoverished population. The return of UNRWA is important not only as a service-provision body but also as an entity that protects the rights and status of Palestinian refugees.

The UN and its associated bodies have established accountability and transparency mechanisms that can minimise the misuse of resources needed for rebuilding Gaza. While ending the occupation depends on the political will of the world’s foremost powers, the UN umbrella maintains the legal status of Gaza as occupied territory and protects the rights of the occupied population.

The UN can also play a role in the deployment of the ISF. The force should be deployed not just in Gaza but also the West Bank to protect Palestinians from settler attacks. Giving the ISF a UN mandate would encourage more countries to contribute to its creation and help build a wider coalition of countries invested in the stabilisation and protection of Gaza and the West Bank. This could be a preliminary step that sets up Israel’s withdrawal from these occupied territories.

The international community must act now. The Board of Peace must be abandoned, and all responsibility for Gaza must be transferred back to the UN system. The UN must be empowered to take the lead in any future arrangements.

Continuing to maintain the current situation in Gaza means the continuation of Palestinian suffering and the deepening of uninhabitability, in effect paving the way for the forced displacement of Palestinians from their land. What is urgently needed is a UN-led mechanism that is immediately enforceable and grounded in international law.



The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Israel’s influence industry in the US
World.content:
Abdul El-Sayed’s hardline campaign exposes a party, a media ecosystem and a debate over Israel in the US.

In the United States, Michigan’s Democratic primary has become a test of how US politics – and the media covering it – are responding to a rapidly changing debate over Israel.

Progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed faces establishment candidate Haley Stevens, whose campaign has attracted unprecedented spending from pro-Israel groups. It is part of a wider trend across the US, as the Israeli government steps up efforts to shape public opinion.

Contributors:

Sarah Leah Whitson – Human rights lawyer

Alex Kane – Senior reporter, Jewish Currents

James Zogby – Founder, Arab American Institute

On our radar

An investigation published by Drop Site News this week has revealed the details of Israel’s latest online influence campaign. Tariq Nafi speaks to the report’s author, Nick Cleveland-Stout, about how the Israeli government is influencing AI-powered chatbots to shape the narrative about the country.

One Sri Lankan monk’s battle against hate speech

For centuries, Buddhist monks have been influential figures in Sri Lanka, advising kings, shaping national identity and mobilising political movements. Today, some have found new audiences as media personalities on YouTube, Facebook and TikTok.

While some monks promote hardline Sinhala-Buddhist nationalist narratives, Galkande Dhammananda Thero is challenging those ideas and offering a different perspective on identity and belonging.

The Listening Post’s Meenakshi Ravi reports on the monks speaking to Sri Lankans from their digital pulpits.

Featuring:

Darshatha Gamage – Digital rights activist

Saritha Irugalbandara – Tech & social media researcher

Galkande Dhammananda Thero – Buddhist monk, Walpola Institute

World.title: From Sudan to Spain: Between war and home | Al Jazeera Originals
World.content:
Aboubaker was 23 when he left Sudan in 2022, hoping for a better future.

This short documentary follows his journey across five countries and the Sahara Desert before he finally reaches Europe. Today, he is rebuilding his life in Madrid through football, work, and a close-knit Sudanese community.

But in April 2023, war broke out in Sudan. As violence continues to engulf his homeland, Aboubaker watches from thousands of kilometres away, desperately awaiting news from the family he left behind in Darfur.

A story about leaving home, finding belonging, and living with the uncertainty of watching a war unfold from afar.

Directed and produced by Chiara Brambilla for Al Jazeera Originals.

World.title: FIFA boss Infantino’s position looks unacceptable: European Leagues head
World.content:
Claudius Schafer says there can be ‘only one consequence’ to Infantino’s actions over his World Cup privatisation plan.

Gianni Infantino’s ‌position as FIFA president looks untenable following his ⁠failed plan to ⁠sell a stake in the World Cup’s commercial rights, the head of Europe’s professional football leagues has said.

Claudius Schafer, whose organisation represents 53 professional men’s and women’s football leagues, said ⁠on Sunday there could be “only one consequence” for ⁠Infantino after his plan triggered a storm of protest from regional associations.

“When I saw how this whole thing unfolded and that FIFA’s key bodies weren’t involved, then there’s essentially only one consequence ‌in any company or association,” he told Swiss newspaper SonntagsZeitung.

Asked if this meant that Infantino was now unacceptable as FIFA president, Schafer said: “This is usually the consequence when someone in a company pushes such a business deal forward without anyone knowing about it.”

Infantino said on Friday FIFA ⁠had scrapped the plan after a widespread ⁠backlash.

Regional confederations UEFA and CONCACAF said on Saturday they had lost confidence in his leadership.

Schafer, also chief executive of the Swiss Football League, said the proposal ⁠suggested that FIFA’s main goal was to maximise profits for third parties by having ⁠more and bigger competitions in future.

“It’s solely ⁠about the financial advantages; everything else is completely ignored,” he said.

The European Leagues opposed this because it would add more matches to an already packed ‌international calendar to the detriment of national championships, Schafer said.



“Nobody knew about the plans, not even the FIFA Council, the governing ‌body ‌of FIFA. I was very surprised that the president was acting completely alone in this matter.”

World.title: Trump Says He Canceled Strikes on Iran, Claiming Progress on Outlines of a Deal
World.content:
President Trump said late Saturday that he had canceled threatened U.S. strikes on Iran, opting to pull back from the brink of renewed war in the Middle East for the second time in two weeks.

Mr. Trump said in a post on social media that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked him to refrain from military action. He also said the “perimeters of a deal” had been reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway for global oil and gas blockaded by Iran for months now.

Iran has yet to give any indication that an agreement to end its grip over the strait was close, and Mr. Trump gave few specifics. The president has repeatedly claimed that Iran’s leaders were on the brink of accepting his conditions without any progress.

But at least one major U.S. ally appeared to have sought to steer Mr. Trump away from the attacks. Saudi state media reported on Sunday morning that Mohammed bin Salman, the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia, recently spoke with Mr. Trump to urge “the necessity of prioritizing dialogue to de-escalate tensions” and “prevent a wider conflict.”

World.title: Cowboys Fringants Bassist Is Named Quebec’s Chief Scientist
World.content:
He’s been described as the Clark Kent-turned-Superman of Quebec.

No horn-rimmed glasses or red capes. But during the day, typically dressed in earth tone blazers, he supervised graduate students and worked on scientific papers on ecological economics. After the sun sets, chest bare and a tie knotted around his head, he played bass guitar before frenzied fans and tossed them beers from the stage.

Across Canada’s French-speaking province, Jérôme Dupras has long been known for his double identity: a well-known expert on the economic value of the environment, who also happens to be a member of Les Cowboys Fringants, or the Dashing Cowboys, one of Quebec’s most famous folk rock bands and the one that best captured the province’s dreams and disillusions of the past generation.

Now the researcher and rock star has assumed yet another identity after the provincial government recently appointed him as chief scientist of Quebec.

World.title: Trump cancels Iran strikes subject to deal being made 'rapidly'
World.content:
Donald Trump says he has cancelled strikes against Iran, provided a deal is struck "rapidly" with the country.

In a post on Truth Social, the US president said he had been asked by Iran and other countries in the Middle East to "hold off" on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.

Trump's comments came after reports that the US and Israel may have been planning new, intense strikes on Iran.

It is not the first time that Trump has issued apocalyptic warnings, only to subsequently insist that diplomacy was being given a chance.

Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency denied that Tehran had asked the US to hold off on further military action, saying Trump's claims were "nothing but a new lie".

Iran's acting Defence Minister Majid Ibn al-Reza said Tehran viewed every threat from its adversaries as "real and credible" even if it formed part of psychological warfare.

"We will neither be caught off guard nor remain passive," he added.

The raised tones followed reports in the US media that the US and Israel were planning what would be one of the harshest bombing campaigns to date against energy infrastructure targets in Iran.

The plan came up during Trump's cabinet meeting on Friday, sources told CBS News, the BBC's News partner in the US.

The US government had also urged Americans across the Middle East to be alert and ready to leave "should there be escalation" in the region.

In his post on Saturday, Trump said the US was "locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II".

He said cancelling the attack would be "for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran".

Back on 7 April, the US president warned that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" if Iran refused to engage in peace talks. He threatened to destroy civilian infrastructure and power plants, a move that many said would be a war crime.

That threat did result in historic face-to-face talks in Pakistan, led by Vice President JD Vance.

For supporters of the president, it was vindication. Bellicose threats - often referred to as the "Madman Theory" - resulted in talks with the Iranians.

The issue with that view, however, is that those talks ended without a deal. There were simply too many competing red lines that could not be reconciled, even with the threat of civilisation erasure.

World.title: How Spain's migrant crisis created a political storm - whipped up by social media
World.content:
Italy is not the only country to see Spain as soft on migration, though.

Meloni's call for an urgent meeting of interior ministers to be held on Tuesday was signed by almost two dozen EU heads of state, calling for the elimination of all policies that could be "pull factors" to Europe.

Above all, they mean Spain's controversial move to allow hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants apply for residence and work permits and "regularise" their status.

The government's pragmatic: Spain is ageing and needs workers.

But those who flocked to the beaches of Ceuta this week were not heading to 

Sanchez himself points instead to a recent ruling by Spain's Supreme Court: it said those who enter by sea cannot be pushed back immediately.

The prime minister argues that was misrepresented by smugglers to promise an easy path to Europe.

The crowd heading for Ceuta didn't need to pay smugglers, though, because most were Moroccan and the route is well known.

The message was actually spread online.

Migrants have shown social media posts to reporters with people shouting that "Spain is Open" and jumping into the sea.

Multiple accounts we've checked ourselves show young people in wetsuits and flippers, or filming themselves already swimming, mixed with pictures from inside Ceuta itself.

Some have only been active for weeks. Several have tens of thousands of likes.

All their promises were false.

The crowds who made it to kiss the shore in Ceuta with joy were met with nothing. Without food or shelter, and with no way on to continental Europe, most quickly turned back.

World.title: Five dead, 41 missing, after Indonesia ferry catches fire
World.content:
Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry carrying at least 250 people caught fire while at sea, officials say.

The captain of the ship reported the fire - off Madura island - as the vessel sailed from the country's second-largest city, Surabaya in East Java, to Makassar in South Sulawesi, according to Basarnas, the National Search and Rescue Agency.

Footage played by local Indonesian news outlet iNews shows large numbers of people in life jackets on what appears to be a lifeboat.

Other clips show people climbing down from the ferry that has flames and plumes of smoke coming from the top of the vessel.

Basarnas posted a video to its TikTok, with a statement saying at 08:24 (02:24 GMT) the Surabaya Search and Rescue office received information that passenger ship KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 was on fire.

"Based on information from the shipping company, the fire occurred at around 06:00-07:00 (00:00-01:00 GMT)."

Later, Basarnas said it got confirmation the ferry "was almost entirely engulfed in flames" as "passengers held on in the ship's bridge and bow while awaiting rescue".

It was unclear how the ferry caught fire, the statement said.

In some of the footage, can be seen jumping into the sea, with crowds of people in life jackets gathering and lifebuoys being thrown to some before they are carried into a rescue ship.

World.title: Young guns for hire - the teenage hitmen recruited to kill across Europe
World.content:
The Natland case illustrates how the VaaS system works.

Natland is the son of two journalists in Stavanger and had a comfortable upbringing, but he drifted into drugs and developed psychosis, ending up spending time in rehab and a short period in a children's home. There he met another teenager who used the online handle UnknownHustler.

It was UnknownHustler who first sent Natland the online request for someone to carry out a hit in the UK - "Killing in England 270k" (270,000 Norwegian kroner is about Â£21,000). It had come from another teenager with the handle Generalen. Generalen - who was 16 at the time and had spent the last three years living in a children's home - subsequently recruited Natland for the hit.

Natland was then passed on to a Foxtrot member with the online username Agent 47, which is borrowed from the Hitman game franchise. Swedish police have accused Ali Shehad Ahmed, who is close to the Foxtrot leader Majid, of being Agent 47.

Agent 47 booked Natland's one way ticket to Manchester Airport, and helped him through the process of getting an emergency passport. Using the messaging app Signal, he guided Natland at every stage of his journey before handing him on to a logistics man with the username "1".

Treating Natland a bit like a character in a computer game, "1" sent him a map and videos showing him where to find the guns hidden in woodland in Huddersfield, and then another video showing him how to access a stash of cash hidden in the undergrowth near a foot tunnel.

Once Natland was installed in his Huddersfield hotel with the weapons, Agent 47 messaged him again: "We have much to do tomorrow."

Natland was arrested the next morning. He had not yet been told who he was to kill, and counterterrorism detectives are still trying to work out whether it was to be a criminal hit or a political one carried out for Iran.

World.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
World.content:
The quickest route for Infantino's exit would be for the Swiss to resign, like his predecessor Sepp Blatter did in 2015.

But Infantino still retains support and he could try to hold out until March, when he is up for re-election for a fourth and final term as president.

What other avenues are open?

The Fifa Council could try to force Infantino's hand through an emergency meeting.

Such a gathering would be triggered if 19 of the 37 Fifa Council members call for one.

Uefa has nine members, AFC has seven, Concacaf five, Africa has six, Conmebol five and Oceania three. It is completed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.

BBC Sport understands there are some doubts that the 19 votes could be achieved.

If they do get to 19, the meeting must take place within two weeks and the Fifa Council could call on Infantino to tender his resignation. But he could simply refuse to do so.

It would, however, add further pressure.

The next step would be an extraordinary congress of the 211 Fifa member associations, which would be held if one-fifth, or 43 associations, "make such a request in writing".

So Uefa, which has 55 nations, can trigger the extraordinary congress whenever it wishes.

That would take a minimum of two months from the point it is triggered, but more likely three months, and there is no guarantee of success.

In effect, it would be a de facto election without there being another candidate as 106 votes would be needed to pass the vote of no confidence.

Uefa has 55, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

Africa, Conmebol and Oceania have not criticised Infantino's plan.

So could Uefa get to 106? In total, 136 countries officially rejected the investment plan, but voting to reject an idea is not the same as voting to kick Infantino out.

Of the 136, Qatar have already publicly backed him and Mexico have distanced themselves from the joint Concacaf statement.

Which leaves finding a suitable candidate to fight the election in March.

Infantino stood unopposed when he was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 and if someone wants to battle him for the position, the deadline to announce their candidacy is 18 November.

World.title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13
World.content:
"Given the severity of the accident, there are no survivors. We have recovered four bodies so far," Police Major Jorge Andrade said, according to AFP.

The crash happened around 13:00 local time (19:00 BST) in the Pueblo Viejo region after the plane departed from an airport in Pisco, Peru.

Video from Reuters news agency shows firefighters spraying water at the scene as smoke rises from the wreckage.

In a statement in Spanish posted online by the Municipalidad Provincial de Nasca, officials expressed "deep sorrow" for the accident and extended "heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased".

The statement said the plane belonged to local Peruvian airline Aerodiana.

In a statement, the airline said it would "assess its flight schedule in accordance with the directives of the relevant authorities", according to Reuters.

The BBC has contacted the airline for comment.

This isn't the first plane to crash over the famed site in the past few decades.

In 2022, another small tourist plane crashed during a flight over the Nazca Lines site, killing seven on board.

And in 2010, a tourist plane went down over the site, killing six people on board.

World.title: Italy putting nearly all major cities on highest heat alert
World.content:
Italy is putting nearly all of its major cities on the highest "red" alert for high temperatures, as a new heatwave grips the country.

Health officials say 19 cities from north to south - including the capital Rome, Milan, Venice and Naples - are already at red alert, and by Monday all but two cities will be.

Temperatures hit mid-30s C in many places on Saturday, and authorities are warning of risks to even healthy and active people - not just groups including the elderly, very young children and people with chronic illnesses.

The warnings come as several European nations battle devastating wildfires after a succession of heatwaves that have created favourable conditions for blazes.

World.title: The Sopranos star Vincent Pastore dies aged 80
World.content:
US actor Vincent Pastore, who played Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero in the hit show The Sopranos, has died aged 80, according to several US outlets.

Pastore was found at his home in the Bronx, New York City and there was no indication of criminality, the BBC's US partner CBS News reported.

In The Sopranos, Pastore played Tony Soprano's best friend who ultimately became an informant for the FBI. His character's death in series two was one of the show's most memorable storylines.

Robert Attermann, Pastore's manager, told CBS News: "To the world, he will always be remembered as the unforgettable 'Big Pussy,' but to those of us who knew him, he was so much more."

World.title: Glasgow 2026: Reporter’s Diary: Day 7-A Super Eagles fan in Edinburgh
World.content:
One of the biggest joys of travelling is meeting people you probably would never have met back home.

A few days into the Commonwealth Games, one of my bosses, Osa Umweni, who used to stay in Lagos, sent me a message.

“So you are 54 minutes by train away from me.”

I smiled.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Umweni now stays in Edinburgh, and before I knew it, an invitation had been extended.

With a break in my Commonwealth Games schedule, I boarded the train from Glasgow for the short journey to Scotland’s beautiful capital.

While waiting for him at Haymarket Train Station, something caught my attention:

Across the station was someone wearing Nigeria’s famous 2018 FIFA World Cup jersey; the green-and-white shirt that became a global fashion statement.

I couldn’t help myself. I crossed over and started a conversation.

His name was Leifson.

He was not Nigerian, but there he was, proudly wearing the Super Eagles jersey in the heart of Edinburgh.

That immediately got my attention.

Leifson told me he was a big fan of Nigerian football, and when I asked about his favourite Nigerian player, he answered without hesitation.

“Odion Ighalo.”

I must admit, I wasn’t expecting that.

We chatted about the Super Eagles, Nigerian football, the World Cup and his love for the beautiful game. He was heading to Glasgow for a concert but was happy to spare a few minutes to talk football with a Nigerian journalist.

Standing there in Edinburgh, thousands of kilometres away from home, football showed again that it truly speaks a universal language.

After my brief but memorable chat with Leifson, Mr Umweni arrived and gave me a warm Edinburgh welcome. He took me to Bonnie and Wild for a treat and was more than ready to help me explore more of the city.

Unfortunately, time was not on my side.

With Nigeria’s medal-winning feats scheduled for the evening session at the Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, I had to rush back to Haymarket Station to catch my train.

I left Edinburgh with a full stomach, a happy heart and another beautiful memory from this trip.

The Commonwealth Games brought me to Scotland for sports, but the unexpected meetings-the taxi drivers, the fans, the strangers who become friends-are adding colour to the journey.

World.title: Africa is rich, doesn’t need aid – Jimoh Ibrahim
World.content:
Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Jimoh Ibrahim, says Africa is a rich continent that does not require aid from other continents to develop.

Mr Ibrahim spoke at a reception in honour of Nigeria’s Ahunna Eziakonwa, who was appointed a Senior Adviser on Africa to the UN Secretary-General António Guterres.

The Nigerian diplomat criticised perceptions of Africa as a beggarly continent dependent on aid.

“Africa consists of 25 per cent of the world population. The future of the world is in Africa. That’s something to talk about,” Mr Ibrahim said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I will not be part of the people who are talking about aid to Africa.

“Africa is made up of sovereign nations; we are independent, and we cannot afford to trade our sovereignty for aid.”

According to him, what Africa needs is trade, collaboration, cooperation and partnership.

“I must thank President Donald Trump for initiating trade and investment as replacements for aid.

“Fantastic programme, so that we can actually capture the essence of our sovereignty and independence.

“I won’t be here to plead for any aid to any African country. We don’t need it. We need collaboration and cooperation and partnership towards human and material development.”

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Africa’s participation in the US government’s new “Trade over Aid” programme remains noticeably low.

Of the nearly four dozen signatories, only six African nations have joined the scheme, with Nigeria taking a prominent but measured role.

Mr Ibrahim also expressed concerns over Africa’s absence on the permanent seats of the UN Security Council.

He noted that Africa was not on the table when nations were negotiating the power make-up of the UN in 1945, as African countries were still being colonised.

“We agreed but over the past 60 years, Nigeria has been a member of the United Nations, we have spent 60 years here, but we haven’t got this permanent seat.

“Africa doesn’t have a permanent seat, and Africa is about 25 per cent of the entire world population.

“If you talk about insecurity, maybe because Africa is not in the permanent seat of the United Nations.”

Mr Ibrahim underscored the importance of Ms Eziakonwa to lend her voice to securing a legitimate permanent seat or seats for Africa in the UN Security Council.

“As adviser on Africa (to the UN Secretary-General), it will be very historic to continue to put your voice at the centre of this engagement,” Mr Ibrahim said.

The ambassador conveyed the goodwill of President Bola Tinubu to Ms Eziakonwa, saying the president was proud and happy about her appointment.

He said he was recently in Nigeria to brief the president about Ms Eziakonwa’s UN appointment and also had lots of discussions about Nigeria and Africa at the UN.

Mr Ibrahim also commended Amina Mohammed, saying Mr Tinubu and the 250 million Nigerians were proud of her achievements as the first woman Deputy Secretary-General of the UN.

Speaking at the event, Ms Mohammed congratulated Eziakonwa on her appointment, saying, “how many aspired to it, but you earned it”.

In her response, Ms Eziakonwa thanked Nigeria for the support through her UN career, saying, “Nigeria is home”.

“This is the country that brought me up. I was educated from birth in Nigeria. We can have all kinds of perspectives about Nigeria today, but Nigeria produced me.

“With all its challenges, I am a product of Nigeria. So all the achievements that you are looking at, the seed was sown in Nigeria. I’m fully made in Nigeria.”

Ms Eziakonwa, a UN assistant secretary-general and UNDP assistant administrator, was, before her new role, the longest-serving Director of the UNDP Regional Bureau for Africa.

(NAN)

World.title: Glasgow 2026: ‘God carried me,’ says Ruth Usoro after Commonwealth Games silver
World.content:
Ruth Usoro has attributed her Commonwealth Games silver medal to divine intervention after overcoming illness and a difficult season to reach the podium in Glasgow.

The Nigerian long jumper, who won silver with a season’s best leap of 6.87 metres, revealed after the competition that she had not been feeling well in the days leading up to the event.

“I haven’t really been feeling so well for some days now. I just have a cough for some reason, and I was wondering how I was going to give my best here. But honestly, the summary of it is that God carried me. I don’t even know how. But here we are,” she told PREMIUM TIMES in Glasgow.

Usoro’s opening jump of 6.87m put her in the lead after the first round before England’s Jazmin Sawyers eventually claimed gold with 6.93m. The Nigerian held on for silver, her first major international outdoor medal.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The result completed a remarkable turnaround for the athlete, who was not originally listed in Nigeria’s squad for the Glasgow Games. She only received a late call-up after long jump star Ese Brume became unavailable.

Reflecting on the unexpected opportunity, Usoro said everything had fallen into place in ways she never imagined.

“I wasn’t supposed to be here, and then I found myself at the Commonwealth Games. Everything has just been glory to glory from there. Then a season’s best yesterday, then another season’s best today. It’s just been amazing.”

A difficult season

Usoro admitted that the 2026 season had been far from straightforward, making the silver medal even more special.

She explained that her focus before the competition was simply to honour God and make those who had supported her proud.

“Going out there, I was just praying, ‘God help me. I just want to bring glory to your name. I just want to bring the medal and make my family, my friends, my coach and my team proud.’ I’m glad this happened. I’m just so thankful to God.”

The silver medal represented a significant improvement on her sixth-place finish at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games and added another medal to Nigeria’s impressive athletics campaign in Glasgow.

Looking ahead

Despite ending the Games on a high, Usoro said she has not yet decided what comes next.

“This season has been a bit rocky. Let’s just see what else God has in store for me.”

She also praised the National Sports Commission (NSC) for improvements in athlete welfare, saying the current environment has helped competitors perform better.

“Things have actually been getting better so far. No doubt we still have a long way to go, like every other country. But compared to how it used to be before, there have been lots of improvements.

“I think at these Games, most of us were in the best mental space that we could be compared to before. I know things can still be better, but I appreciate what they are doing.”

Usoro’s silver is one of several medals won by Team Nigeria’s athletics team in Glasgow, where the country remains Africa’s highest-ranked nation on the Commonwealth Games medals table.

World.title: Nigeria deploys 86 troops to ECOWAS peace mission in Guinea-Bissau
World.content:
The Nigerian Army has deployed 86 troops to the ECOWAS Stabilisation Support Mission in Guinea-Bissau (ESSMGB), reinforcing Nigeria’s commitment to regional peace and security and its longstanding role in peace support operations across West Africa.

In a statement posted across its official social media pages on Saturday, the army explained that the troops, who were deployed as Nigerian Company 5 (NIGCOY 5 ESSMGB), departed the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard a Nigerian Air Force C-130 Hercules aircraft and arrived safely in Guinea-Bissau to begin their assignment under the ECOWAS mandate.

Before they departed from the Nigerian Army Peacekeeping Forward Operating Base in Abuja, the army’s Chief of Operations, Mayirenso Saraso, a major general, urged the personnel to maintain the highest standards of professionalism, discipline and operational excellence throughout the mission.

Represented by the Director of Peace Support Operations, MM Idris, a brigadier general, Mr Saraso charged the troops to serve as worthy ambassadors of the army, the Armed Forces of Nigeria and the country by faithfully executing their mandate, respecting the laws and customs of the host nation, and maintaining zero tolerance for sexual exploitation and abuse, substance abuse, indiscipline and the irresponsible use of social media.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The army said the deployment highlights Nigeria’s continued commitment to regional stability and its leadership in ECOWAS peace support efforts.

It added that it remains one of Africa’s leading contributors to regional and international peacekeeping missions, drawing on decades of service under ECOWAS, the African Union and the United Nations.

According to the army, the latest deployment reflects Nigeria’s strategic role in conflict prevention, peacebuilding and post-conflict stabilisation across the continent through the professionalism and resilience of its peacekeepers.

Background

The ESSMGB was established to support security sector reforms and help preserve political stability in Guinea-Bissau following years of political crises and repeated military interventions.

READ ALSO: Nigeria hails ECOWAS backing for African Atlantic Gas Pipeline

The mission succeeded the ECOWAS Mission in Guinea-Bissau (ECOMIB), which had been deployed after the 2012 coup, and forms part of the regional bloc’s efforts to prevent instability from escalating into wider regional security threats.

Nigeria has consistently been one of the largest troop contributors to ECOWAS peace support operations, providing personnel, logistics and leadership for missions across West Africa, including Liberia, Sierra Leone, The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau.

The latest deployment comes as ECOWAS faces growing security and political challenges across West Africa, including military takeovers in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, as well as persistent jihadist violence in the Sahel.

While Guinea-Bissau has largely avoided the scale of violence seen elsewhere in the region, ECOWAS continues to maintain a stabilisation presence to support constitutional order and deter potential security disruptions.

World.title: Iwobi scores as Fulham fight back to beat Farense in Pre-Season test
World.content:
Super Eagles midfielder Alex Iwobi was on target as Fulham came from behind to secure a 2-1 victory over Portuguese outfit Farense in their final pre-season fixture of the club’s training camp in Portugal on Saturday.

The Nigeria international delivered another assured performance in midfield, playing a pivotal role as Álvaro Arbeloa’s side wrapped up their preparations for the new campaign with a morale-boosting comeback win.

Fulham found themselves trailing at the interval after Farense struck first in the opening half, forcing the Premier League side to mount a response after the restart.

Their breakthrough arrived when Emile Smith Rowe was brought down inside the penalty area, with Iwobi confidently stepping up to take responsibility from the spot.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Super Eagles star made no mistake, calmly sending the goalkeeper the wrong way before drilling his penalty into the corner to draw Fulham level and swing the momentum in his side’s favour.

Buoyed by the equaliser, Fulham dominated the closing stages as they searched for a winner, and their persistence was rewarded in dramatic fashion just before full-time.

In the 89th minute, Josh King was fouled inside the penalty area to hand the Cottagers another spot-kick. Brazilian forward Rodrigo Muniz converted with confidence, firing into the same corner as Iwobi to complete the turnaround and seal victory for the Premier League club.

The result capped an encouraging pre-season for Fulham ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, with Iwobi once again underlining his importance to the team.

The Nigerian midfielder enjoyed another impressive season last term, registering four goals and three assists in 29 Premier League appearances while establishing himself as one of Fulham’s most reliable performers, despite the club narrowly missing out on European qualification.

Having carried his impressive form into pre-season, Iwobi will now be aiming to maintain that momentum when Fulham begin their 2026/27 Premier League campaign, as he looks to play an even bigger role in the club’s push for a return to European football.

World.title: INTERVIEW: I wanted to become Nigeria’s first men’s 100m Commonwealth champion, says Kayinsola Ajayi
World.content:
Kayinsola Ajayi added another milestone to his remarkable 2026 season by winning a bronze medal in the men’s 100m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The medal made him the first Nigerian man in two decades to reach the podium in the event at the Games. Fresh from the medal ceremony, the 21-year-old spoke to PREMIUM TIMES about his performance, his quest for gold, the upcoming 4x100m relay, staying grounded amid growing fame, and representing his Ikorodu neighborhood.

Question: Congratulations. You’ve just collected your bronze medal in the men’s 100m. You’re smiling today. Has it started to sink in how special this achievement is?

Kayinsola Ajayi: Yeah, I mean, even after yesterday’s race, a lot of people were congratulating me and telling me they enjoyed watching me compete. They kept saying, “You did your best.” So, yeah, I’m proud of myself, and I feel like everybody was happy. I was also happy with the performance I put on yesterday, especially with the rain and the weather. I feel like I can’t beat myself up forever.

Question: You’re now the first Nigerian man to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the 100m in two decades. How does that feel?

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Kayinsola Ajayi: Yesterday, I went out there with the mindset of becoming the first Nigerian man to win gold in the 100m at the Commonwealth Games. I wanted to win so badly. I really wanted that gold. But I’m grateful to come away with a medal.

Question: You’re only 21. Does that give you confidence that your best years are still ahead?

Kayinsola Ajayi: I still have a lot of time. I’m only 21, so I just have to keep working, keep trusting myself, and keep trusting God.

Question: One of your major goals this season was the individual 100m. Now your attention shifts to the 4x100m relay. What is the plan?

Kayinsola Ajayi: Me and the boys are ready. You know how we get. We’re ready for the 4x100m. On Saturday, we’re going to put on a show. We’re just going to trust God and let Him take control.

Question: It’s been an incredible season for you. You broke the Nigerian record, equalled it twice and also won on the Diamond League circuit. How do you reflect on your progress?

Kayinsola Ajayi: I’m proud of myself for doing that. I’m on the right path and doing the right things. I’m consistent, and that’s part of being a good athlete. So, yeah, I’m proud of myself.

Question: At one point this season, you were the world leader and your name was everywhere. How do you stay grounded despite the growing attention?

Kayinsola Ajayi: After the race, I just go back to my normal self. I don’t feel like I’m bigger than anybody. At the end of the day, you just have to humble yourself. You don’t have to let all of that get into your head.

Question: Each time your achievements are celebrated, especially by Making of Champions, people also talk about Ikorodu. How does it feel to be putting your hometown on the global map?

Kayinsola Ajayi: I feel great about it. People always say, “Ikorodu to the world,” and I’m proud to be part of that. It feels good to know you’re putting Ikorodu on the map. Some people think that because you’re from Ikorodu, you can’t make it, but that’s a big lie. If you’re disciplined, you know what you’re doing, you trust yourself and trust God, everything will work out. It doesn’t matter where you come from. You can make it.

Question: What comes next after Glasgow?

Kayinsola Ajayi: One step at a time, like I always say. I’ll go back to school, get back to work, keep training, and take it from there.

World.title: Glasgow 2026: Fatima Yusuf-Olukoju hails Ella Onojuvwevwo after ending Nigeria’s 32-year medal drought
World.content:
Former Commonwealth Games silver medallist Fatima Yusuf-Olukoju has congratulated Ella Onojuvwevwo after the youngster ended Nigeria’s 32-year wait for a medal in the women’s 400 metres at the Commonwealth Games.

Onojuvwevwo won bronze at the Glasgow 2026 Games, clocking 51.00 seconds to finish behind Jamaica’s Dejanea Oakley and Barbados’ Sada Williams.

The medal was Nigeria’s first in the event since Yusuf-Olukoju claimed silver at the 1994 Commonwealth Games in Victoria, Canada.

Celebrating the achievement in a heartfelt Facebook post, Yusuf-Olukoju praised the 21-year-old for restoring Nigeria’s presence in one of its traditional athletics events.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Love you Onojuvwevwo Ella!!! ❤️🇳🇬 You officially broke the curse and brought home a 🥉, making Nigeria’s women’s 400m relevant again! 💪🏾 Thank you for reminding the world that Nigerians still know how to sprint one full lap without asking for directions. 😅🏃🏾‍♀️

“The future is incredibly bright. Keep making us proud—we’re all cheering you on! 🇳🇬🔥 #LA28.”

Ending a long wait

Onojuvwevwo’s bronze carries historical significance for Nigerian athletics.

Before her podium finish in Glasgow, Nigeria had gone more than three decades without a Commonwealth Games medal in the women’s one-lap event.

The country’s last medallist was Yusuf-Olukoju, who won silver in Victoria in 1994, four years after she captured Nigeria’s first and only Commonwealth Games gold in the event at Auckland 1990.

By claiming bronze in Glasgow, Onojuvwevwo became only the third Nigerian woman to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the women’s 400m, joining Yusuf-Olukoju and Charity Opara, who earned bronze during Nigeria’s memorable one-three finish at the 1990 Games.

A hopeful sign for Los Angeles

Beyond ending the Commonwealth medal drought, Onojuvwevwo’s achievement has also sparked optimism ahead of the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

The Los Angeles Olympics will mark 32 years since Falilat Ogunkoya won Nigeria’s last Olympic medal in the women’s 400 metres at the Atlanta 1996 Games.

With a new generation led by Onojuvwevwo emerging on the international stage, many Nigerian athletics followers hope history could repeat itself.

World.title: Nwabali returns in style, wins man-of-the-match, after eight-month absence
World.content:
Super Eagles goalkeeper Stanley Nwabali marked his return to competitive football in emphatic fashion, earning the Man of the Match award as Chippa United held Golden Arrows to a goalless draw in their opening fixture of the 2026/27 South African Premier Soccer League season on Saturday.

Making his first competitive appearance in eight months, the 30-year-old produced a commanding display at the King Goodwill Zwelithini Stadium, reminding fans and selectors alike of the qualities that established him as one of Africa’s finest goalkeepers.

According to FotMob, Nwabali finished the match with a 9.1 rating; the highest of any player on the pitch, after making six crucial saves to secure a valuable clean sheet for the Chilli Boys.

The Nigerian shot-stopper only returned to Chippa United last month after previously leaving the club following Nigeria’s AFCON 2025 campaign in Morocco, with both parties agreeing to terminate his contract by mutual consent.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

His comeback follows a difficult period off the pitch during which he openly spoke about battling mental health challenges after the heartbreaking loss of both parents.

Against Golden Arrows, however, Nwabali looked every bit the goalkeeper who inspired the Super Eagles to continental success.

Despite Chippa United spending long periods without the ball as Golden Arrows dominated possession and created the better chances, the Nigerian remained unbeatable throughout the contest.

His standout moment came just before the hour mark when he produced a stunning double save to deny Ronaldo Van Neel, preserving parity with a brilliant display of reflexes and positioning.

Beyond his outstanding shot-stopping, Nwabali was instrumental in organising Chippa United’s defensive unit. He marshalled his backline with authority, claimed crosses confidently and reacted sharply to dangerous loose balls inside the penalty area.

His all-round performance included three high claims, three clearances and an impressive 12 ball recoveries, although his passing accuracy of 65 per cent highlighted an area the experienced goalkeeper will look to improve as the season progresses.

Nwabali announced himself on the continental stage during the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations, where his heroics helped Nigeria reach the final of the tournament and saw him displace Francis Uzoho as the Super Eagles’ first-choice goalkeeper.

He also did well with the Super Eagles at the AFCON 2025 edition in Morocco where Nigeria won a record-extending bronze medal.

However, his departure from Chippa United and subsequent spell without a club saw him lose his place in the national team to Maduka Okoye.

Saturday’s performance could prove to be a timely reminder to Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle that Nwabali remains a serious contender for the number one jersey ahead of Nigeria’s upcoming international assignments.

For Chippa United, who finished just three points above the relegation zone last season, the draw represents a solid start to the new campaign.

The Chilli Boys will now turn their attention to their next league fixture, where they host Richards Bay on 11 August, with Nwabali hoping to build on a dream return between the posts.

World.title: ‘I was dollar millionaire at 30, at 35 I was working as a labourer’ — Farooq Oreagba
World.content:
Businessman Farooq Oreagba, popularly known as Mr. Steeze, has reflected on the highs and lows of his financial journey, revealing that he went from being a dollar millionaire at the age of 30 to working as a labourer in England just five years later after losing his banking job.

Oreagba made the revelation during an appearance on Ebuka Obi-Uchendu’s MENtality show, co-hosted by Banky W, where he spoke about wealth, materialism and the importance of life over money.

During the conversation, Oreagba posed a hypothetical question to Ebuka to illustrate his belief that life is more valuable than any amount of wealth.

“Ebuka I’m going to drop a few nuggets here. How much is money to you. Will a billionaire dollar satisfy you?” he asked.

Responding, Ebuka said, “I’m not looking for satisfaction.”

Oreagba continued, “Okay now I’m going back to the first question about materialism and people chasing money but if I gave you 10 million dollars now, what would you say?”

Ebuka replied, “What would I say? I’ll call you from Miami to thank you.”

Oreagba then added, “But what if I told you you can have it but not live more than 24 hours to spend it what would you do?”

Ebuka responded, “I mean I could make 10 million dollars, so it’s not worth it.”

Using the exchange to make his point, Oreagba reflected on his own experience with wealth and

hardship.

“Right. Then all of a sudden living now has more value. I was a dollar millionaire at 30, at 35 I was working as a labourer in England. I had my dream and all them I lost my job as a banker. To maintain that lifestyle I was hustling, doing all kinds of stuff… I had my priorities wrong. Sometimes we place priorities on….”

Oreagba said the experience taught him that many people spend too much time chasing money while neglecting what truly matters, noting that wealth alone does not define the value of life.

World.title: How many African countries will qualify for Women’s World Cup through WAFCON?
World.content:
Super Falcons

The 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco will not only crown the continent’s champions but also determine which African teams will book their places at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

With Africa’s allocation increased for the expanded Women’s World Cup, the continent has a chance to send up to six teams to the global tournament.

How many African teams will qualify?

A total of four African countries will qualify automatically for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

These will be the four semifinalists at the 2026 WAFCON. Once a team reaches the semi-finals, it secures a direct ticket to Brazil.

In addition, two more African nations will have another opportunity to reach the World Cup by competing in the FIFA inter-confederation play-offs.

This means Africa could ultimately have as many as six representatives at the 2027 Women’s World Cup if both play-off teams successfully qualify.

How qualification works

The 2026 WAFCON features 16 teams, divided into four groups of four.

The qualification process is as follows:

Four groups of four teams each.

The top two teams in every group advance to the quarter-finals.

The four quarter-final winners progress to the semi-finals.

Those four semi-finalists qualify automatically for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

The two losing quarter-finalists with the best overall tournament performance will earn places in the FIFA Women’s World Cup play-offs.

WAFCON 2026 tournament details

Host: Morocco

Dates: July 26 – August 16, 2026

Teams: 16

Groups: Four groups of four teams

Automatic World Cup qualification spots: Four

Inter-confederation play-off spots: Two

Africa’s possible representatives at Brazil 2027

Depending on the results, Africa will have:

4 teams guaranteed at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

Up to 6 teams if both play-off representatives secure qualification.

World.title: Top 10 countries paying highest minimum wages in 2026
World.content:
Minimum wage policies differ widely around the world, with some countries guaranteeing workers more than three times what others pay for the same number of hours.

While higher wages are often linked to a country’s cost of living, productivity and labour laws, they also reflect efforts to ensure workers can maintain a decent standard of living.

Several high-income economies continued to raise their wage floors in 2026 to keep pace with inflation and labour market pressures, with European nations dominating the rankings.

Below are the 10 countries offering the highest statutory minimum wages in 2026, based on official national rates. U.S. dollar conversions are approximate and based on exchange rates in early 2026.

1. Luxembourg

Luxembourg continues to top the global rankings with the highest statutory minimum wage. The country adjusts its wage floor in line with inflation and conducts formal reviews every two years. Workers with recognised qualifications earn more than the standard minimum.

2026 minimum wage

Skilled workers (18+): €3,244.48 per month (about $3,792 )

(about ) Unskilled workers (18+): €2,703.74 per month (about $3,160)

2. Australia

Australia remains among the world’s best-paying countries for minimum wage earners. The national rate is reviewed every year by the Fair Work Commission, while employers are also required to make compulsory superannuation contributions on behalf of workers.

2026 minimum wage

A$24.95 per hour (about US$16.87 )

(about ) Equivalent to roughly US$2,830 per month for full-time employment

3. Ireland

Strong economic growth and regular wage adjustments have helped Ireland maintain one of Europe’s highest minimum wages. The country ranks among the leading employers in terms of statutory pay.

2026 minimum wage

€2,391 per month (about US$2,794)

4. Germany

Germany continues to strengthen worker protections through regular increases to its national minimum wage. The latest adjustment benefits millions of employees, with another rise already planned for 2027.

2026 minimum wage

€13.90 per hour (about US$16.24)

5. Netherlands

The Netherlands updates its minimum wage twice each year, allowing workers’ earnings to reflect changing economic conditions. Holiday allowances also provide additional income beyond regular wages.

2026 minimum wage

€14.71 per hour (about US$17.19)

6. Belgium

Belgium combines a national minimum wage with sector-specific agreements that often guarantee even higher pay. The country’s wage system is supported by strong collective bargaining.

2026 minimum wage

€2,154.11 per month (about US$2,517)

7. United Kingdom

The UK’s National Living Wage increased again in 2026 as part of the government’s commitment to maintaining wages at around two-thirds of median earnings for eligible workers.

2026 minimum wage

£12.71 per hour (about US$16.82)

8. New Zealand

New Zealand reviews its minimum wage annually, with the rate applying to most workers aged 16 and above. The country remains one of the highest-paying labour markets in the Asia-Pacific region.

2026 minimum wage

NZ$23.50 per hour (about US$13.38 )

(about ) Approximately US$2,335 per month for full-time workers

9. France

France’s minimum wage, widely known as the SMIC, is automatically adjusted to account for inflation and broader wage trends, helping preserve workers’ purchasing power.

2026 minimum wage

€1,823.03 per month (about US$2,130)

10. Canada

Canada rounds out the top 10, although it does not operate a single nationwide minimum wage. Instead, each province and territory sets its own rate, resulting in significant differences across the country.

2026 minimum wage

C$15.00 to C$19.75 per hour, depending on the province (about US$10.84 to US$14.28 per hour)
