World.title: Paarl Gimnasium beat Paarl Boys’ High in world’s biggest schoolboy derby
World.content:
Paarl Gimnasium continued their outstanding 2026 season by claiming derby bragging rights with a commanding victory over Paarl Boys' High. Image: Instagram @paarlgim1858

Paarl Gimnasium continued their outstanding 2026 season by claiming derby bragging rights with a commanding 25-11 victory over Paarl Boys’ High in front of a packed Faure Street Stadium on Saturday.

A crowd of approximately 25 000 witnessed Gimmies score four tries, with outside centre Derik Cloete producing a man of the match performance by crossing twice as his side secured a 15th consecutive victory following their only defeat of the season.

Left to rue missed chances

Boishaai made the stronger start and raced into a 6-0 lead through two penalties from Daniel Mesenheimer, but were left to rue several missed attacking opportunities that could have increased their advantage.



Gimmies gradually settled into the contest, with Louis Koen opening their account from the kicking tee before Cloete produced a moment of individual brilliance.

The outside centre chipped over the defence, regathered superbly and finished in the corner to hand the visitors a 10-6 lead at the break.

Slick move

The second half belonged to Gimmies.

Cloete grabbed his second try after a slick backline move before Thomas Saunders produced one of the moments of the match, sprinting 55 metres and beating three defenders to stretch the advantage to 20-6.

Boishaai briefly threatened a comeback when winger Aleit Stander crossed from a quick-tap penalty while Gimmies lock Dirk Hugo was serving a yellow card.

Any hopes of a late fightback were extinguished in the closing stages when scrumhalf Mickyle Booise collected a superb offload from winger De Waal Vivier to score Gimmies’ fourth try and seal an impressive 25-11 triumph.

World.title: Four men killed in Nyanga shooting
World.content:
Police investigate the fatal shooting of four men in Nyanga. Image: Pexels

Police have launched a murder investigation after unknown gunmen shot and killed four men in Nyanga, Western Cape, on Saturday night.

The attack happened at about 9:55pm on Old Klipfontein Road after the men stopped to fix a flat tyre on their Toyota Avanza.

Gunmen opened fire

Police spokesperson Colonel André Traut said the victims were repairing the tyre when the attackers struck.



“Preliminary reports indicate that at approximately 21:55, the victims were travelling in a Toyota Avanza along Old Klipfontein Road when they stopped to repair a flat tyre. While they were attending to the vehicle, they came under attack by unknown gunmen who opened fire on them,” said Traut.

Paramedics declared all four men dead at the scene after they suffered multiple gunshot wounds.

Taxi violence suspected in deadly shooting

The gunmen fled the scene before police arrived and remain at large.

Police believe the attack may be linked to the taxi industry. Investigators on the other hand are still working to establish the exact motive.

The Serious Violent Crime Unit has opened four murder cases and is leading the investigation.

Police appeal for information

Police have urged anyone with information about the shooting to come forward.



Members of the public can contact the SAPS Crime Stop number on 08600 10111 or submit anonymous tips through the MySAPS mobile application.

Police will treat all information in the strictest confidence.
