World.title: Center Party leader backs temporary border controls over migration concerns
World.content:
Center Party chair Mihhail Kõlvart backs temporarily restoring border controls in the Schengen area, saying Estonia must also prioritize security over free movement slogans.

In a social media post on Saturday, Kõlvart pointed to Spain's Ceuta migration crisis as a warning of how quickly border pressures can escalate. He said decisions by authorities and courts had contributed to a situation where tens of thousands of people entered Europe within a short period.

"We can speculate about how much of this happened unintentionally and to what extent someone from the outside deliberately contributed to it, but in any case, it showed how easily such a crisis can emerge and escalate," he said, adding that migration pressure has also been used as a hybrid tactic against Europe.

Kõlvart said these recent events also serve as a reminder that in a crisis, every country must first look after its own interests. He cited Italy's temporary restoration of border controls with Spain as an example.

"Estonia, too, must also put its own interests first and prioritize its own security," he stressed.

The opposition party chair criticized Prime Minister Kristen Michal's (Reform) recent statement that free movement in Europe is a top priority and that temporarily reinstating Schengen border controls is not in Estonia's interests, calling the stance a slogan disconnected from reality.

"Free movement does not outweigh the need to mitigate the security threats Europe is currently facing," Kõlvart said.

'Estonia isn't prepared for this'

He also dismissed the prime minister's calls to hold those organizing the migration accountable as just rhetoric, saying things have already spiraled out of control and the damage has already been done in Spain.

"Unfortunately, we have to acknowledge that Estonia currently isn't prepared for migration crises like this either," Kõlvart said, warning that even a crisis a fraction of that size would be catastrophic for Estonia.

"This does not mean that everyone should fend for themselves in difficult times or that no one should help an EU member state in need," he continued. "Of course we must help Spain, but Spain itself must also take appropriate steps toward resolving this crisis, and take steps to prevent it from happening again."

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform). Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Kõlvart said the issue cannot be addressed by allowing problems to spread across Europe. While acknowledging that many migrants who arrived in Spain have since left, he said guarantees are needed that further migration waves will not follow.

"Until then, temporarily restoring border controls is a necessary and justified step," he concluded.

PM supports Spain, rejects border controls

Approximately 60,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco this week. As of Friday evening, more than 48,000 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco, Spanish officials said.

The influx comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish enclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Michal signed a joint letter with 21 other member states addressed to the EU's top leaders on Saturday calling for "an immediate and coordinated European response."

Responding to comments from opposition Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu, the prime minister also pushed back on the suggestion that suspending free movement within the EU's Schengen area would be justified in such a critical situation.

Calling the Schengen area a "great value," Michal wrote on social media that establishing new internal borders within it is in no way in Estonia's interests.

"None of us wants to return to a time when traveling overland to Central Europe meant passing through more than five cumbersome border checks," he said.

World.title: Gallery: Setos elect new leader at one-day Seto Kingdom
World.content:
In a traditional direct vote at Seto Kingdom Day in Mikitamäe, Setos and guests elected local culture advocate Ingrit Kala the next ülembsootska, or leader of the Seto people.

Now in its 33rd year, the annual Seto Kingdom Day in Southeastern Estonia returned to Mikitamäe on Saturday, where sprawling grounds at the heart of the village were packed with celebrations, contests and showcases of the Seto language, food, culture, history and people.

The event culminated with the direct election of a new ülembsootska, chief regent of the Seto god-king Peko and ceremonial leader of the Seto people.

Thousands of people took part, lining up in front of their preferred candidate and gripping a rope extending from each to cast their vote.

Kala defeated fellow candidate and former nuursootska, or youth regent, Rain Oper, by a margin of several hundred supporters.

Succeeding Jalmar Vabarna, Kala will be joined in her role as leader of the Setos for the year by returning nuursootska Maria Grünberg, who was elected by children and teens the day before.

The 33rd Seto Kingdom Day took place in Mikitamäe on Saturday. August 1, 2026. Source: Leevi Lillemäe/ERR

"You have to be there for your own people, of course, and when you are invited somewhere, you go and bring them your blessing," said Kala, noting that it's important to work beyond the Seto community as well, to boost their visibility.

Kala added that developing and preserving the local Seto language would be one of her priorities as ülembsootska, noting that fewer people speak it today.

"Especially for young people, so that the Seto language doesn't disappear completely," she emphasized.

'There's always something'

Local resident Signe said Seto Kingdom Day brings together not just Setos, but those who feel connected to the Seto identity as well.

"I haven't lived here long — this is now my second year living in Setomaa," she said, adding that she had followed her heart to the region.

For Signe, one of the most important parts of the annual celebration is that it brings people together, reconnecting familiar faces and giving them a chance to catch up.

"There's always something," she added. "It's the little things that make it a wonderful day."

World.title: Warning signs now required before mobile speed cameras in Estonia
World.content:
Police in Estonia must now post warning signs before mobile speed cameras, even as officials disagree on what happens if a sign is blown over or removed.

Legislative amendments that took effect on August 1 require police to post warning signs 150–300 meters ahead of mobile speed cameras in town and 300–600 meters ahead of them on highways.

Taavi Kirss, head of traffic enforcement at the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), said officers will post signs as required and document their locations before starting speed enforcement.

"Everything depends on where we can carry out speed enforcement," Kirss said. "Where we can position ourselves and where the mobile speed camera can be placed. From there, we can determine where the warning sign can be placed."

Police record when signs are installed but cannot monitor them continuously. If one is blown over by wind or removed by someone, the officer operating the camera may not even know.

According to Kirss, however, drivers would still be required to pay any resulting fine.

"We have installed the sign as prescribed by law; we've done everything required on our end," he said.

The Interior Ministry is less certain, and expects a number of legal challenges until a court ruling settles the matter. Legal adviser Rina Sillandi said disputes would likely have to be resolved based on the evidence in each case.

"Unfortunately, it's difficult to say how this will end up working in practice," Sillandi said.

Attorney: New signs are unnecessary

Attorney Indrek Sirk said documenting when signs are installed and removed should reduce disputes, especially since mobile speed checks are typically conducted for short periods.

Nonetheless, he called the new requirement unnecessary.

"This was a propaganda measure," Sirk said, noting that some people will certainly like to see police powers limited in certain areas. "But generally speaking, I see no benefit whatsoever, for either the rule of law or traffic safety, in posting these road signs."

Mobile speed cameras have been vandalized three times this year, with offenders liable for the damage. Each repair has cost €20,000.

World.title: Schengen Area must be preserved, says Estonia's PM
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) has said the European Union must jointly act on migration after the crisis in Spain this week and that the Schengen free movement area must be preserved.

Approximately 60,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco this week. As of Friday evening, more than 48,000 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco, Spanish officials said.

The influx comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish enclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Michal signed a joint letter with 21 other member states addressed to the EU's top leaders on Saturday calling for "an immediate and coordinated European response."

"We cannot allow uncontrolled mass crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration or other hybrid threats to create the perception that illegal entry into the European Union is possible. That a migrant's illegal entry can turn into legal stay," the statement says.

It added that ministers should consider enhanced support from the EU's border force, Frontex, and "the effectiveness of EU cooperation with Morocco."

Estonia, together with 21 other Member States, calls on @eucopresident, @vonderleyen, and @MichealMartinTD to take immediate action to jointly support Spain in restoring effective control of the EU's external border.



Europe must respond with unity to uncontrolled mass crossings,… pic.twitter.com/RxMdi8zBKh — Kristen Michal (@KristenMichalPM) August 1, 2026

The letter was signed by representatives from Italy, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Sweden.

Schengen Area 'must be preserved'

He also responded to comments from the chairman of the opposition party Isamaa, Urmas Reinsalu, who said suspending the Schengen free movement zone would be justified in such a critical situation, as Italy temporarily did with Spain earlier this week.

Writing on social media, Michal said: "The creation of new internal borders within the Schengen Area is in no way in the interests of Estonia or Estonians. None of us wants to return to a time when travelling overland to Central Europe meant passing through more than five cumbersome border checks."

Michal stressed that Estonia treats every illegal border crossing with the "utmost seriousness" and is already helping other countries, such as Latvia, with their border issues.

"Those who organize such migration will be punished, and those who arrive in Estonia illegally will be detained and sent back to the countries they came from," he wrote.

"The Schengen Area is a great value that must be preserved."

'Full solidarity with Spain'

Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200). Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

While other countries took to social media to criticize Spain on Friday, Estonia's Minister of Foreign Affairs sent a message of solidarity.

"The developments in Ceuta are deeply concerning. Estonia stands in full solidarity with Spain as it faces unprecedented migration pressure," Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) wrote on social media.

"Spain has both the right and the responsibility to protect its borders – and the European Union's external border. No one has the right to enter the European Union without abiding by our common rules. Respect for those rules is essential to safeguarding the integrity of the Schengen Area," he continued.

World.title: Police will not control queue 'place buying' at Narva border
World.content:
The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) and the Ministry of Interior are not planning to crack down on people selling places in the queue at the Narva border crossing as wait times increase due to summer tourism to Russia.

The Ministry of the Interior and the PPA said they are aware that places in the queue are being sold around the Narva border crossing, Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) acknowledged in response to a question submitted by MP Aleksandr Tsaplõgin (Centre Party).

Queues at Estonia's land borders increase considerably in the summer as Russians living abroad and international tourists visit Russia. Flights from Europe were suspended following the start of the full-scale invasion, and Finland closed its borders after migration pressure several years ago. Estonia has also reduced the operational hours at the border to 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

Taro noted that the queue forms in a public space and that there are no regulations governing the line. "The PPA monitors the situation from the perspective of public order and safety. If violations or conflicts arise, the police intervene," he said.

The minister confirmed that the police assess every report indicating possible organized crime. "If specific cases contain indications of threats, extortion or other criminal activity, they are investigated and, if necessary, proceedings are initiated. It has not been confirmed that this involves a criminal group," he noted.

Minister of the Interior Igor Taro. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

The police have received reports concerning the area around the Narva border crossing, but they do not amount statistically to the volume or pattern that would indicate a widespread, systematic wave of violence or extortion.

"Reports involving threats, the risk of violence or damage to property are reviewed and, where necessary, misdemeanor or criminal proceedings are initiated if the legal grounds are met," Taro said.

In 2025, the police received 46 reports that places in the queue were being sold at Peetri Square in Narva. This year, they have received 16 such reports. Last year, there were 62 reports of public order violations, while this year the number stands at 17," the minister said.

"At the same time, it cannot be said that all of these reports are related to the border queue. Over the past two years, seven offense reports have been filed. In two cases, criminal offenses involving either theft or causing bodily injury were reported, while the remaining five involved misdemeanors, including damaging another person's property, consuming alcohol in a public place, or disobeying or insulting officials."

No proceedings have been initiated on the basis of reports about selling places in the queue. The situations have been resolved by Narva police officers, and those selling places in the queue have been removed from the line, Taro added.

Peetri plats in 2024. Source: Jenny Va / ERR

'Avoid travelling to Russia'

Asked why, despite the well-known problem, there is no permanent police presence or regular patrols near the border crossing to prevent unlawful activity, Taro replied that the law does not assign the police the task of organizing the queue of pedestrians crossing the border in a public space.

"However, the police are responsible for maintaining public order. Around the Narva border crossing, patrols and police presence are deployed on a risk-based basis where there is a greater threat to public order or security. Maintaining a permanent stationary police presence wherever a queue forms is neither practical nor proportionate. If conflicts or the threat of violence arise, people can call 112, and the police will respond," the minister said.

Tsaplõgin also asked what specific measures the Ministry of the Interior intends to take to stop the illegal sale of queue places.

"The PPA will continue to maintain public order through risk-based patrols and by responding to specific incidents. People are continually reminded of the complexity of crossing the border and the need to take into account long waiting times, restrictions and unexpected changes to border crossing procedures," Taro said.

Adding: "As a representative of the government, I support the recommendation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and likewise advise people to avoid travelling to Russia altogether!"

World.title: Raul Meel's anniversary exhibition on display at the Poco Ajamaja gallery
World.content:
Dedicated to Raul Meel's 85th birthday, the exhibition "Concret" is open at the Poco Ajamaja gallery. It traces the artist's journey from his first groundbreaking experiments in the late 1960s to the present day.

Exhibition curator Jaan Heinsoo says the exhibition focuses on concrete poetry – works that combine poetry and visual art. In concrete poetry, meaning is not only derived from words but also from visual experience, the rhythmic structure of words and signs, the interplay of colors, repetition, and silence.

"The exhibition is a retrospective of the artist's life's work spanning more than fifty years, presenting a cross-section of the various eras, facets, and techniques of Raul Meel's creative journey from 1970s typewriter drawings to a painting from the "Epic of Bristles" series created this year," Heinsoo explained.

"A large portion of the works were produced over the past year, yet the ideas and motifs largely originate from earlier creative periods."

Meel (b. 1941) is one of Estonia's best-known avant-garde artists and among Europe's leading practitioners of conceptual art and concrete poetry. He has participated in more than 600 group exhibitions and over 100 solo exhibitions, and remains the only Estonian artist to have received a prize at a major international biennial.

World.title: Zaidi threatens to resign as Coordination Framework divided over response to Saudi strikes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reportedly threatened to resign during a recent meeting of the Coordination Framework amid deep divisions over how Iraq should respond to recent Saudi military strikes, according to a report published Sunday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada.

Citing political sources, the newspaper said the prime minister’s remarks came during a tense meeting that exposed growing disagreements among senior Shiite leaders over security policy, the role of armed factions, and Baghdad’s handling of escalating regional tensions.

According to the report, the meeting became increasingly heated after intelligence was presented alleging that the armed group Saraya Awliya al-Dam was preparing to launch an attack against Jordan from Iraqi territory. The sources said Amman had warned Baghdad it would respond to any attack originating from Iraq, further intensifying the debate.

The report claims the dispute centered on whether Iraq should adhere to the government’s official position or allow individual armed factions to respond independently to the recent Saudi strikes. While most Coordination Framework leaders reportedly backed the government’s approach, one influential figure with ties to Saraya Awliya al-Dam insisted on carrying out a unilateral response.

Al-Mada reported that armed factions have given the government until next Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia. According to the sources, they warned that if Baghdad fails to act, they may launch their own response.

The newspaper also reported that the escalating dispute prompted al-Zaidi to again raise the possibility of resigning, marking what would be the second time he has reportedly made such a threat since taking office. According to the report, he previously suggested stepping down if his anti-corruption agenda failed.

The sources further claimed that the prime minister is facing mounting political pressure, including concerns about his personal security, although no official statements have confirmed those assertions.

The report also focused on the investigation into drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, stating that seven Iraqi-Saudi security meetings, with U.S. participation in some sessions, have been held over the past two months.

According to Al-Mada’s sources, the investigations have not produced conclusive evidence proving that the attacks originated from Iraqi territory, despite Saudi accusations.

The report said several scenarios remain under discussion, including the possibility that Iraqi armed factions were responsible, that Houthi operatives present in Iraq facilitated the attacks, or alternative theories promoted by some factions alleging Israeli activity in Iraq’s southern desert regions.

According to the newspaper, the ongoing crisis led al-Zaidi to cancel a planned visit to Saudi Arabia, which Iraqi officials reportedly viewed as an opportunity to attract much-needed Saudi investment at a time when Iraq faces mounting financial pressures.

The report also said armed factions have urged the prime minister to suspend efforts to bring all weapons under state control, arguing that the recent Saudi strikes have fundamentally altered the security landscape.

Al-Mada also reported that discussions during the meeting touched on the role of Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Faleh al-Fayyadh during the recent U.S.-Saudi strikes that targeted PMF facilities.

According to the newspaper’s sources, claims circulated that al-Zaidi had warned al-Fayyadh upon returning from Turkey that PMF sites could be targeted, and that evacuation efforts were delayed. However, other participants reportedly dismissed those claims, suggesting they reflected internal political disputes rather than established facts.

The Iraqi government has previously denied having prior knowledge of the U.S.-Saudi strikes. Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad neither approved nor was informed in advance of the attacks.

However, U.S. President Donald Trump later told Fox News that the strikes had been coordinated with the Iraqi government, presenting an account that differs from Baghdad’s official position.

World.title: Zaidi’s failed raid on Nujaba base exposes challenges in disarmament push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A failed security operation targeting a facility belonging to the Iran-aligned Harakat al-Nujaba movement has underscored the challenges facing the Iraqi government as it seeks to bring all armed groups under state control before the end of September.

According to a report published by Al-Monitor, a joint Iraqi force attempted to search a Harakat al-Nujaba compound in Baghdad’s Jurf al-Naddaf district on July 24 after receiving intelligence suggesting the site contained missiles and drones. However, the operation ended without the facility being searched after armed members of the group confronted government forces.

The report, citing Iraqi security officials, said the operation involved Baghdad Operations Command, the Federal Police, and the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Security Directorate. Shortly after arriving at the compound, commanders affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba reportedly ordered their fighters to prevent security personnel from entering. Armed members of the group then surrounded the government force and fired warning shots into the air, forcing the operation to halt.

According to the officials, the PMF leadership subsequently instructed its personnel to withdraw, stating they had not been informed that the target was a facility affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba. Army units involved in the operation later received similar withdrawal orders. No casualties were reported, and neither the government nor the armed group publicly disclosed details of the incident at the time.

The incident comes as Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has pledged to ensure that all weapons in Iraq are brought under state control by September 30, the scheduled end of the U.S.-led coalition’s military mission in the country.

Al-Monitor described the failed operation as the first significant field test of the government’s commitment to enforcing that pledge. While previous administrations also announced plans to limit weapons to state institutions, implementation has remained difficult due to the political and military influence of several armed factions.

Hayder al-Shakeri, a researcher with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, told Al-Monitor that although Baghdad has increasingly relied on restructuring security institutions and applying political and financial pressure on armed groups, the Jurf al-Naddaf operation demonstrated the limits of the state’s authority when confronted directly.

“If the government cannot enforce its decisions against a single armed faction, or fails to follow through with legal and political accountability, it suggests that these groups still retain an effective veto over certain state actions,” Al-Shakeri was quoted as saying.

The report noted that not all Iran-aligned factions share the same position regarding government efforts to centralize weapons under state control.

Some groups, including Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have become increasingly integrated into Iraq’s political and economic systems, potentially reducing their willingness to engage in direct confrontation. Others—including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada—continue to oppose any move that would place their military capabilities under full government authority.

Political analyst Muhannad al-Ghazi told Al-Monitor that these factions view their weapons through an ideological lens, making voluntary disarmament highly unlikely. He argued that targeting isolated weapons caches without addressing broader military infrastructure would have only a limited impact.

The reported confrontation occurred amid heightened regional tensions following Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s recent visit to Washington, where Iraq and the United States announced a strategic economic partnership.

According to Al-Monitor, several Iran-backed factions criticized the visit, warning against what they described as replacing “military occupation” with “economic occupation” through expanded U.S. investment in Iraq.

The report also linked the incident to broader regional developments, including recent drone attacks and cross-border military operations that have intensified pressure on Baghdad’s efforts to assert control over its territory.

Al-Monitor concluded that the government’s September 30 target for fully disarming armed factions appears increasingly difficult to achieve given current realities.

Instead, analysts cited by the publication believe Baghdad may focus on more gradual measures, including relocating some weapons, closing selected facilities, and increasing political and financial pressure on groups willing to cooperate, while avoiding direct confrontation with the most heavily armed factions.

The report suggested that the ultimate success of Iraq’s disarmament strategy may depend not only on domestic enforcement but also on broader regional dynamics, particularly relations between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Jordan threatens to strike Iranian militias in Iraq if they launched attacks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Amman has publicly warned Iraq that it will launch military operations against Iran-backed militias if they attack Jordan.

The warning comes after a rapid increase in regional violence, including recent interceptions of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones over Jordanian airspace, which targeted US installations.

An official Jordanian source told Al-Arabiya News that Jordan provided Iraq with precise intelligence indicating that pro-Iran militants are planning to strike Jordanian territory.

Jordan has publicly said that it expects the Iraqi government to take quick and effective measures to curb these armed groups.

Jordanian sources identify front organizations such as Awliya al-Dam as key players in these border-threatening actions.

The warning represents a strong change in Jordan’s defensive stance in the face of rising tensions between the United States and Iran.

Jordan harbors critical Western military installations, such as the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, which have become active targets for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its allies in the region.

Jordan emphasized that, while it aims to avoid regional escalation, it considers national sovereignty and border security to be inviolable priorities.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey sign deal to transport 750,000 barrels of Iraqi oil to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Turkey have formally inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired last Monday.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi stated that both countries are developing a more comprehensive bilateral framework. This initiative is likely to include cross-border collaboration in the water, electricity, and oil sectors.

The pipeline has a maximum capacity of 1.5 million barrels per day. However, due to legal issues between Baghdad, Erbil, and Ankara, it is currently operating at a capacity ranging between 170,000 and 200,000 barrels per day.

Al-Zaidi described the deal as an important milestone that will protect Iraq’s economy from rising regional crises. Following his high-level diplomatic visit to Ankara, the agreement reestablishes energy transit stability between the two countries.

World.title: Chevron CFO bullish on Iraq after West Qurna 2, Nassiriya agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chevron boasts “significant potential” to expand its activities in Iraq over the next decade, according to Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner, highlighting the US oil company’s increasing trust in the country’s energy sector after recent deals with Baghdad.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Bonner said that Iraq remained one of Chevron’s top priority markets for future production expansion after the signing of preliminary agreements to pursue negotiations on the massive West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya oil fields.

She added that Chevron has been encouraged by its interaction with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Iraq’s Ministry of Oil while discussions continue and that the corporation is also collaborating with Baghdad on diverse crude export routes to boost Iraq’s long-term energy security.

The statements bolster rising trust among foreign energy corporations after Al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States earlier this month, during which Iraq inked more than $60 billion in investment deals covering energy, infrastructure, banking, and technology.

World.title: Syria joins Saudi Arabia, Jordan in warning Iraq over Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Syria has joined Saudi Arabia and Jordan in warning Baghdad that strikes conducted from Iraqi soil against neighboring nations may result in military strikes against the armed groups responsible, according to Syrian military officials cited by regional media.

According to Al Jazeera and the US-funded Al Hurra, a senior Syrian military source said that Damascus will react to any strikes from Iraq by attacking the “terrorist militias” involved inside Iraqi territory.

The purported warning comes amid a steep increase in regional tensions after US-Saudi bombings against Iran-backed militias in Iraq in retaliation for drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were conducted from Iraqi territory.

The Iraqi government has frequently said that it would not allow Iraqi land to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring nations.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi recently issued an order establishing a comprehensive security strategy aimed at enhancing state authority and preventing armed organizations from endangering regional security.

The new threat puts further pressure on Baghdad, as more neighboring nations indicate they may take direct action if cross-border assaults continue.

Iraqi authorities have attempted to prevent such a situation, claiming that security activities should be overseen by the Iraqi government rather than foreign forces.

Several Iran-backed organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are at the heart of the conflict, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security system, some of its sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have been accused by regional governments of carrying out strikes outside of Baghdad’s jurisdiction.

For Iraq, the diplomatic stakes go beyond security.

Baghdad has been attempting to reestablish ties with Syria as part of greater regional economic integration, including talks on resurrecting the old Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to the Mediterranean, which is considered strategically crucial for diversifying Iraq’s export routes outside the Gulf.

The purported Syrian warning comes at a critical moment for Al-Zaidi’s administration, which has spent recent months bolstering relations with Washington, Ankara, Riyadh, and Damascus while portraying Iraq as a secure destination for global investment.

The mounting threats from neighboring Arab governments highlight the importance of Baghdad demonstrating its ability to prevent armed groups from conducting strikes independent of the state.

Failure to do so risks increasing regional military tensions and jeopardizing Iraq’s aspirations to boost commerce, energy cooperation, and infrastructure projects with its neighbors.

The Syrian government has not issued an official warning, and IraqiNews.com has not independently confirmed the statements ascribed to the Syrian military source.

However, the claims reflect rising regional worry that strikes by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil could further destabilize the area and hamper Iraq’s diplomatic and economic goals.

World.title: Iran-backed militias threaten Iraq’s ties with US and Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Escalating tensions between Iran-backed militias are providing one of the most serious hurdles yet to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s ambitions to deepen ties with the United States and Gulf states while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

The most recent crisis followed US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, when Saudi Arabia accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones at oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Riyadh claimed that the operation targeted the militias responsible for the assaults rather than the Iraqi state or its military forces, but Baghdad denounced the strikes as a breach of national sovereignty.

The recent tensions are being fueled by numerous prominent Iran-aligned organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), notably Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its groups have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and have occasionally conducted operations outside of Baghdad’s chain of command.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi responded by calling an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, canceling a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and announcing a comprehensive security strategy to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring countries.

The administration also reiterated its resolve to keep all weapons entirely under state control.

That vow has gained importance after Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington earlier this month, during which Iraq and the United States reiterated their commitment to completing the US-led coalition operation by the end of September 2026.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi pledged to ensure that all weapons eventually come into the control of the Iraqi state, citing it as a cornerstone of his government’s security strategy and a crucial step toward bolstering Iraq’s sovereignty and stability.

Since entering office, Al-Zaidi has maintained a policy of balancing Iraq’s ties with rival regional and international forces.

During recent travels to Washington, Ankara, and Tehran, he achieved huge investment and cooperation deals totaling tens of billions of dollars in the energy, banking, technology, infrastructure, and industrial sectors.

His administration has also attempted to strengthen connections with Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and other Gulf nations via new transportation corridors, energy alliances, and trade agreements aimed at diversifying Iraq’s economy beyond oil and positioning the country as a regional center linking the Gulf to Europe.

According to analysts, Baghdad’s approach is highly dependent on proving that the Iraqi state, rather than armed groups, controls the country’s security and foreign policy.

Continued strikes from Iraqi territory risk eroding the country’s reputation with major regional allies and international investors, at a time when foreign investment has risen after years of turmoil.

The stakes rose when US President Donald Trump said that recent US-Saudi operations against Iran-backed militias were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim Baghdad has denied.

Observers believe it reflects rising discontent among Iraq’s leadership with armed groups accused of dragging the nation into regional conflicts that contradict Baghdad’s diplomatic and economic interests.

Al-Zaidi is currently facing the most significant test of his leadership.

Delivering on his promise to place all weapons under state control will be critical not only for Iraq’s internal security but also for maintaining trust with the United States, Gulf Arab states, and international investors, many of whom support many of the country’s largest economic projects.

Baghdad’s dilemma now extends beyond managing ties between Washington and Tehran.

It demonstrates that the Iraqi state possesses both the authority and the political will to prevent Iran-backed militias from using Iraqi territory to launch attacks that risk isolating the country, harming relations with Arab neighbors and the United States, and jeopardizing Iraq’s long-term economic recovery and investment goals.

World.title: Iraq faces growing fiscal strain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is under increasing financial strain as plummeting oil earnings tighten government budgets, with Health Minister Abdul Hussein al-Mousawi saying that ensuring monthly public-sector wages has become the government’s top priority.

Speaking at a public meeting, al-Mousawi stated that the government requires approximately 10.8 trillion Iraqi dinars ($8.2 billion) per month to pay public-sector salaries, while current monthly oil revenues have fallen to approximately 2.5 trillion dinars, highlighting the growing gap between government obligations and income.

The statements are one of the most direct public acknowledgements by a top Iraqi official of the government’s financial challenges after months of decreased oil prices and fewer export profits.

Iraq’s government finances remain very vulnerable to variations in global energy markets because the vast bulk of public revenue comes from crude oil.

Official figures published this week indicated that oil accounted for over 84% of federal income in the first five months of 2026, but collections decreased by more than one-third compared to the same time the previous year as oil prices and export profits plummeted.

The health minister also warned of financing restrictions in the healthcare sector, citing worries about the supply of medications and the government’s capacity to sustain public services if financial pressures continue.

The fresh warnings follow weeks of increased regional tensions, which disrupted oil markets and added uncertainty to Iraq’s economic prospects.

As OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq relies on oil exports to fund wages, pensions, social welfare, and the majority of government expenditure, making the budget susceptible to long-term reductions in crude prices.

Economists have long cautioned that Iraq’s reliance on oil income makes the nation susceptible to external shocks, while a hefty public-sector pay bill constrains the government’s budgetary flexibility.

Previous administrations attempted to diversify income streams via tax changes and non-oil investments, but hydrocarbons remain the economy’s backbone.

The financial pressure comes at a critical time for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government, which has been promoting Iraq as a destination for billions of dollars in foreign investment following agreements signed with US, Turkish, and international companies in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

Continued budgetary strain may make it more urgent to accelerate economic reforms, raise non-oil income, and improve public financial management to lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

They also emphasize that preserving investor trust will be contingent on the government’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability while continuing to fund big development projects.

Despite the present issues, Iraq has large foreign currency reserves, which act as a financial cushion for the government.

However, experts warn that while reserves might help absorb short-term shocks, they are not a substitute for the fundamental changes needed to diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on unpredictable oil earnings.

World.title: 'Kerala stands united': Rahul Gandhi offers support as rains claim 8 lives, leave 8 missing
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader

on Sunday expressed deep sorrow over the devastation caused by heavy rains in Kerala, offering condolences to the families of eight people who lost their lives and urging party workers to assist in relief and recovery operations.

"Deeply saddened by the devastation caused by heavy rains across Kerala. My heartfelt condolences to the families of the eight people who have lost their lives. May those still missing be found safe, and the injured make a swift recovery," he said in a post on X.

The Congress leader also added that the state government was making every possible effort to support affected families and coordinate relief operations. "I urge all Congress workers and volunteers to assist these efforts in every possible way," he said, urging people to remain vigilant, especially in hilly regions, and follow authorities' guidance.

"Kerala stands united in this difficult hour. I stand firmly with every affected family," Rahul Gandhi added.

Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan confirmed that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 others injured in the heavy rains that triggered landslides, waterlogging and property damage across the state. In a statement, he said 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to 209 relief camps.





Satheesan said that despite a reduction in rainfall, people should remain vigilant, especially in hilly areas. He said the government would ensure assistance to families of the deceased and those who lost homes and livelihoods.

Revenue minister A P Anilkumar told reporters the situation was improving and was under control. He said damaged roads had been restored in many areas, though some restrictions on vehicular movement remained.

He added that alerts had been issued for several districts and preparations were in place.

According to the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, the state received up to 320 mm of rainfall in some parts on Saturday, with Ayyankunnu in Kannur district recording the highest. The rains inundated low-lying and riverside areas, especially in Pathanamthitta, Idukki, Wayanad, Kottayam, Kozhikode and Kannur districts.

IMD issued an orange alert for 12 districts and a yellow alert for Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam, warning of flash floods in all districts between 2 pm and 8 pm. Heavy rainfall was predicted on August 2, 3 and 6, with strong winds of up to 50 kmph.

The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services warned of huge waves of 2.7 to 3.5 meters along the northern Kerala coast and advised fishermen and coastal residents to be vigilant.

On Sunday morning, while rains subsided, water had not receded from flooded areas, with people seen travelling using small boats. The water level in some power generation dams in Idukki, Pathanamthitta and Thrissur districts remained in red alert status, according to KSDMA.

State tourism minister P C Vishnunadh said an additional NDRF team was deployed for rescue efforts in Pathanamthitta and Aranmula, with fire force units from Thiruvananthapuram, Palakkad and Ernakulam. Fishermen and fishing boats were also deployed for quick response.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Indonesia ferry fire kills 5, rescue teams recover Nirmal Purja's body & more
World.content:
At least five people died and 41 remain missing after a passenger ferry caught fire off Madura Island.

Rescuers recovered Nirmal Purja 's body after the avalanche, with all 10 climbers now confirmed dead.

Here are the top news stories:



Indonesia ferry fire : 5 dead, 41 missing after blaze engulfs passenger vessel

At least five people died and 41 remain missing after the passenger ferry KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 caught fire off Indonesia's Madura Island while carrying around 250 people. Several passengers jumped into the sea as nearby vessels rescued survivors.

More than 200 people have been evacuated, while rescue operations continue. Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire.







Nimal Purja's body found after deadly avalanche that killed 10 climbers

The body of legendary mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja has been recovered after a deadly avalanche struck Broad Peak in PoK, with all 10 members of the expedition now confirmed dead. Rescue teams continue efforts to recover the remaining bodies despite difficult weather. Purja, famed for climbing all 14 peaks above 8,000 metres in a record 189 days, is being remembered as one of mountaineering's greatest figures.



'Mekedatu is permanent solution': Karnataka CM pushes Cauvery dam project

Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar called the Mekedatu dam project the "permanent solution" to the Cauvery water dispute and urged all stakeholders to move forward. He cited recent Supreme Court rulings and the Centre's position while appealing for dialogue with Tamil Nadu. The project remains opposed by Tamil Nadu over concerns about downstream water availability.

Lovlina flags missing Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's India map

Commonwealth Games silver medallist Lovlina Borgohain objected after noticing that the Northeast was missing from an India map printed on napkins and displayed outside a Glasgow restaurant.





The Assam boxer said the omission "hurt us" and raised it with the management, which admitted the mistake and promised to correct the branding immediately.

FPIs return to Indian equities with Rs 20,200 crore July investment

Foreign portfolio investors returned to Indian equities in July after four months of continuous selling, investing Rs 20,200 crore. Analysts attributed the comeback to attractive valuations, stronger corporate earnings, rupee stability and improving global sentiment. FPIs also invested heavily in India's debt market, although they remain net sellers for the year overall.

World.title: Students from around the world experience the Jain way of life in Rajasthan
World.content:
Nestled amid the arid plains of Rajasthan, about 230 miles west of Delhi, Ladnun is the kind of town many travelers might pass without a second glance. Its narrow streets, whitewashed temples, and unhurried pace stand in stark contrast to Indiaâs bustling metropolitan centers.

This summer, however, the quiet town has become an unlikely destination for seekers of one of the worldâs oldest philosophies.

For more than three centuries, Ladnun has been the spiritual home of the Terapanth order of Jainism, a reformist sect known for its disciplined monastic tradition and emphasis on nonviolence, self-restraint, and spiritual inquiry. Last month, those traditions welcomed an unusual group of visitors: nearly three dozen students, scholars, and faculty members from eight countries who are spending three weeks not merely studying Jainism, but living it.

The immersive summer program, which began July 20 and concludes on Friday, is the result of a collaboration among Florida International University, California State University Long Beach, the Jain Education and Research Foundation (JERF), Jain Visva Bharati Institute, and southern California philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose support made the initiative possible.

Rather than treating Jainism as an academic subject confined to classrooms and textbooks, the organizers designed a program that allows participants to experience the philosophy through daily practice.





Each morning began with meditation. Students attended lectures on Jain philosophy, Prakrit â the ancient language of many Jain scriptures â and the foundational principles of âAhimsaâ (nonviolence), âAnekantavadaâ (the multiplicity of viewpoints), and âAparigrahaâ (non-attachment to possessions). They also interacted with monks and nuns, observed their disciplined routines, and experienced a lifestyle centered on simplicity, compassion, and mindfulness.

âIt has been a very eventful week, and it has been a tremendous experience,â said Anne Vallely, a professor at the University of Ottawa and one of the foremost scholars of Jainism in the Western world.

Describing the demanding schedule, she added, âWe have our lessons from 9:00 in the morning, and they go really into 10 oâclock, 11:00 at night.â

The program reflects months of planning by scholars in India and the United States.

Florida International University, home to the first endowed chairs in Jain Studies in the United States, worked closely with California State University Long Beach, to develop the curriculum. The Jain Education and Research Foundation helped coordinate the academic and logistical aspects of the initiative, while Jain Visva Bharati opened its sprawling campus and monastic community to the international participants.

At the heart of the effort is a broader mission: introducing Jain philosophy to a global audience at a time when its central teachings of nonviolence, environmental sustainability, restraint, and respect for diverse perspectives have taken on renewed relevance.

Much of that vision has been championed by physician, entrepreneur, and philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose years of support for Jain education and higher learning have helped establish academic programs across the United States.

Modi, who has contributed tens of millions of dollars to educational and religious causes in the United States, India, and globally, provided the principal financial support for this yearâs summer school.

âI was born in India in the Jain faith, and those principles of Ahimsa, compassion, and respect for all living beings have guided my entire life as a physician,â the La CaÃ±ada, California,-based physician entrepreneur told The American Bazaar.

ââ After my medical career, I realized philanthropy allows me to heal on a larger scale, not just one patient at a time. I contribute to Jain education because I believe Americaâs young students must be exposed to this ancient wisdom of tolerance, non-possessiveness, and plurality, which is so undervalued today.

â

The program also coincided with another milestone.

This year marks the 300th anniversary of the founding of the Terapanth order, giving participants an opportunity to witness commemorative events while learning about one of Jainismâs most influential traditions.

Established in the 18th century by Acharya Bhikshu, the Terapanth order is distinguished by its centralized leadership and disciplined monastic structure. Its monks and nuns travel extensively to spread Jain teachings rather than remaining in permanent monasteries.

Throughout the three weeks, students discovered that learning extended far beyond formal lectures.

Meals became lessons in mindful eating. Silence became a form of reflection.

Conversations with monks and nuns often continued long after scheduled sessions ended. Participants learned not only the philosophical foundations of Jainism but also how those principles shape everyday decisions, from food and consumption to conflict resolution and environmental responsibility.

For many students, the immersive setting transformed abstract ideas into lived experience.

âIâm surrounded by scholars and Iâve gotten to meet with sadhvis and sadhus, and itâs just been lovely,â said Carol Rodriguez, one of the participants, who holds a Ph.D.

in Jain Studies from the University of Florida.

The Cuban-born scholar earned her bachelorâs and masterâs degrees in Jain Studies from Florida International University in Miami, where she translated portions of the Lilavatisara, a 13th-century work by Jain monk Jinaratnasuri.

The international composition of the group further enriched the discussions. Participants brought diverse academic backgrounds and cultural perspectives, creating conversations that reflected Jainismâs emphasis on dialogue and multiple viewpoints rather than absolute certainty.

Organizers hope the program will serve as a model for future international collaborations in religious studies, philosophy, sustainability, and peace education.

Unlike traditional study abroad programs, the Ladnun initiative invites participants to become temporary members of a living spiritual community, where learning occurs as much through observation and daily practice as through formal instruction.

As the summer school concludes on July 7, participants will return to universities and communities around the world carrying more than lecture notes and academic credits. They will leave with firsthand experience of a philosophy that has quietly endured for millennia and memories of a small Rajasthan town where, for three weeks, Jainism was not simply studied, but lived.

Dhage

contributed to the report.)

World.title: 'Ready to face death': Pappu Yadav defiant after FIR over Ram Temple donation 'theft' skit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Independent MP

on Sunday remained defiant after Varanasi Police registered a case against him, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

and Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Awadhesh Prasad over a Parliament skit depicting the alleged theft of donations from the Ram Temple in

, Uttar Pradesh.

Pappu Yadav, whose real name is Rajesh Ranjan, said he was "ready to face death" to protect people's faith from those who "betray Sanatan and God."

"If Pappu Yadav has to die to protect the faith of the people of Sanatan and India against those who betray Sanatan and God, I step out every day ready to face death," the Lok Sabha MP from Bihar's Purnia seat told reporters on Sunday.

"Do I not have the right to wear saffron?... Rahul Gandhi was never afraid of an FIR; Priyanka Gandhi was never afraid; so how could Pappu Yadav be afraid?" he asked.

Pappu Yadav's remarks came a day after Varanasi Police registered an FIR against him, Rahul Gandhi and Awadhesh Prasad following a complaint by a religious leader. Another complaint has also been filed against the Purnia MP by petitioner Surya Maithil at Jehangirpuri Police Station in the national capital.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The controversy centres on Friday's demonstration, during which Pappu Yadav, dressed in saffron robes as a temple priest, and other opposition MPs staged a skit involving a donation box and allegations of corruption.





He portrayed a temple priest collecting offerings from devotees while holding a photograph of Lord Ram. Fellow opposition leaders played devotees who came forward to place donations in a collection box.

In a scripted sequence, the "priest" was shown pocketing the money instead of depositing it in the box, following which a Samajwadi Party MP, playing a devotee, confronted him over the "illegal" act.

The performance prompted BJP leaders, including MP Bansuri Swaraj and several MLAs, to file formal police complaints in New Delhi, accusing the opposition leaders of hurting Hindu religious sentiments. The saffron party heads the government at the Centre and is also in power in Uttar Pradesh, which is set to go to polls early next year and where the BJP has been in office since March 2017.

World.title: The towel on the chair: How it became India's ultimate status symbol
World.content:
Long ago, my father told me a story about a certain â

ji. Nobody ever addressed him by his first name, it was always succeeded by a âjiâ, because his office chair was covered with a towel.

He would often wear a safari suit & a stiff-upper lip at family weddings. The guy with a govt job, an Afsar (officer), top billing in the arranged marriage market, despite having the lowest basic pay. At one such wedding, his wife blurted out an issue they were facing. Due to some clerical mistake, the details of their salary account was not updated, and Sunil ji wasnât receiving his salary for over 2 years. They found this anomaly just last month.

My family was grudgingly impressed, and hoped one of their kids turned out to be a towel-chair guy like Sunil ji.

For much of modern Indiaâs history, there wasn't enough. Jobs. College seats. Telephones. Gas cylinders. Batsmen with a good strike rate. We were short of everything. As if our nation came out of British rule like some of the TV reporters came out of the NEET protest, Gasping for breath, barely surviving the violence with almost all of the valuables stolen, but their morality, virtue and the associated pride intact.





This was India in 1947.

Such was the muscle memory of the rule, that we kept presenting our Annual budget at 5 PM IST, so that our British overlords could tune-in after having their breakfast. This tradition continued till 1999, more than 50 years after independence, until the Finance minister

, changed it to 11 AM. Imagine. The trauma of British rule never went away, it showed up in our metabolic wiring, in our insulin resistance, in our early onset of diabetes.

Primarily due to the British administered famines. The bodies of our ancestors rewired to store fat. When the Brits eventually went back, they left behind quite a few problematic things like bureaucracy, Pakistan & monumental scarcity.

When our leaders took over, they knew our demand vastly exceeded the supply, so they had to control the access of resources. And who do you trust to do that?

Another British inheritance - The Collectorate. A regiment of people specifically trained to extract from the population, to collect revenues and give it back to the overlords, for whom serving people was optional, a hobby.

A lot of them were corrupt too, In contrast there was barely any corruption among British officers, because they were paid almost 70 times the Indian officers. Hence, the Indians had to compensate with corruption.

As we know, they continued compensating beyond independence as well. This coterie was assigned to allocate resources to Indians.

No wonder, they acquired tremendous power. People began paying to jump the queue.

When the government decided who could manufacture, import or expand a factory, permissions themselves became valuable commodities. British raj was eventually succeeded by Inspector Raj. And the underpaid inspectors lived in the same bungalows the British lived in.

Economist Robert Klitgaard famously summarized it as:

Corruption = Monopoly + discretion - accountability

Whenever one person has monopoly over a decision, wide discretion, and little accountability, corruption happens.

Accountability was like Vitamin-D for the country. We were always deficient. Add to that a lethargic judiciary. Some even justified corruption saying it's an essential lubricant for files to move without friction. A tool to facilitate ease of doing business. Many of the Indian billionaires today, exist due to their ancestors greasing their file-folders with this lubricant generously.

Corruption is a chronic illness, it has been embedded in the DNA of a drought-coded, resource starved nation like ours.

A government comes to power riding a wave of public anger. The previous regime is portrayed as irredeemably corrupt. Files are opened. Committees are formed. Raids happen. People are content. Finally, someone is cleaning the system.

For a while, it genuinely feels different. Time passes, Power stops feeling temporary. The government begins winning elections. The public approval remains high. Loyalists become more confident.

Criticism starts sounding less like feedback and more like conspiracy. Every institution gradually fills up with people who think alike.

Corruption creeps up again. Like a virus - a parasite that needs a host - like a mosquito or a bat or a pigeon.

Parasites don't advertise themselves. They attach themselves to something stronger. In India's case, this host is often identity - caste, religion, language. Every political movement needs an emotional engine.

That engine mobilises voters, creates loyalty and builds political capital. Most of the time these issues are legitimate and deeply important. But once emotions become intense enough, they also become excellent camouflage.

People stop asking uncomfortable questions because larger battles appear to be underway.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

If my religion is under threat, why discuss the waterlogged street near my house?

If my caste is finally receiving justice, why focus on procurement irregularities?

Not saying, Identity is not important. But we often forget to see whatâs lurking behind it.

The virus keeps growing, and one day it becomes bigger than the host, voters can see it, and it gets overthrown. Exit pollsters get shamed. The power of democracy is lauded. Until a new host emerges. The cycle continues. Elections just change the wrapper of the age-old system.

Corruption will go away when we make it high-risk and low-reward. High salaries & high conviction rate. A Singaporean minister earns more than a top investment banker. And their corruption watchdog has a conviction rate of 99%. Our ED has at ~1%. This is the crux, until we fix it - another Sunil ji will discover they have a salary account a decade later.

Abhishek Asthana is a tech & media entrepreneur. He runs a creative agency called GingerMonkey & is also the Co-founder of

Knot Dating

, a VC funded matrimony startup.

World.title: 158 exam irregularity cases await trial; CBI seeks fast-track disposal under new anti-paper leak law
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Around 158 cases related to alleged recruitment examination irregularities are pending trial in courts across the country despite the completion of investigations, with some cases dating back more than two decades, PTI reported.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), which probed these matters, has decided to approach high courts seeking the transfer of pending cases to fast-track courts being set up in several states to handle cases under the new anti-paper leak law.

The agency will inform the high courts that it would provide dedicated special prosecutors and make all possible resources available to ensure the earliest possible conclusion of the trials.

Government officials attributed the delays to the transfer of investigating officers, prosecutors, and even presiding judges.

Which state accounts for how many cases



Delhi accounted for 25 alleged irregularity cases registered since 2000. These include the AIIMS PG recruitment examination case of 2010-11, the Delhi University Medical and Dental Entrance Examination case of 2011, CAT (Common Admission Test) irregularities of 2004, the SSC (Staff Selection Commission) recruitment case of 2013, and teachers' recruitment cases.





Bihar has five pending cases, including three linked to the alleged NEET 2024 paper leak, besides irregularities in the PMT (Pre-Medical Test) examinations of 2003 and 2011.

In Himachal Pradesh, the 2022 constable recruitment case is among three cases awaiting the start of trial. Jammu and Kashmir also has three pending cases, including alleged irregularities in junior engineer and constable recruitment.

Similarly, five cases are awaiting trial in Jharkhand, five in Karnataka, three in Maharashtra â including two related to NEET 2024 â eight in Rajasthan, 14 in Tamil Nadu, and 10 each in West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh.

New anti-paper leak law



The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026, recently passed by Parliament, provides for every state and Union territory to designate a sessions court as a special fast-track court in consultation with the chief justice of the concerned high court.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The law mandates that these fast-track courts hear cases on a day-to-day basis without unnecessary adjournments, with trials to be completed within three months of the filing of the charge sheet.

It also provides for the transfer of cases already pending before other courts to these newly designated special fast-track courts, where they are to be concluded within three months of transfer.

Every state and Union territory will also appoint dedicated special public prosecutors to represent these cases.

The legislation was enacted in the wake of the recent student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, which culminated with the resignation of the-then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak in May. Protesters had also called for wider reforms in the country's examination system, following which the government constituted a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to recommend reforms.

World.title: 'Mekedatu project is permanent solution': Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar on Cauvery water dispute with Tamil Nadu
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

DK Shivakumar on Sunday described the Mekedatu dam project, proposed by the state government on the Cauvery river, as a "permanent solution" to the long-standing dispute between Karnataka and neighbouring Tamil Nadu over the sharing of Cauvery river water.

"The Mekedatu project is the permanent solution. The Supreme Court has already delivered its judgment, and the central government has also given its response. Taking all that into consideration, we should move forward without wasting any more time," he said at a press conference after chairing an all-party meeting on the Cauvery water issue, which has flared up again in recent days.

The chief minister was referring to the Supreme Court's

of Tamil Nadu's objection to Karnataka's detailed project report on the Mekedatu project.

In May this year, the top court also rejected Tamil Nadu's review petition challenging the earlier judgment.

The Centre, meanwhile,

Parliament in July that the Supreme Court's order does not state that Karnataka requires Tamil Nadu's consent for any new construction across the Cauvery river.

Shivakumar further urged all stakeholders to move forward without wasting any more time, taking the developments into consideration.





"Taking all that into consideration, we should move forward without wasting any more time. This is not about Tamil Nadu getting more or Karnataka getting less. We should use this opportunity to bring both states to the table, hold discussions, and resolve the issue amicably. We expect everyoneâs cooperation in this effort," the Congress leader added.

The Cauvery water dispute revolves around how the river waters should be shared between the two states, particularly during years of low rainfall.

The issue resurfaced amid developments concerning the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, proposed by Karnataka. It has been a major point of friction between the two states, with Tamil Nadu traditionally opposing it on the grounds that it would affect the flow of water downstream.

The latest tensions have emerged at a time when the Congress is part of the TVK-led new state government in Tamil Nadu. The party was also an ally of the DMK, the previous ruling party, but extended only external support to the government.

World.title: 'He will not be taken back': Mayawati expels former MP Ashok Siddharth from BSP again
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati on Sunday announced the expulsion of former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddarth from the party, less than a year after

him in September 2025.

Mayawati said Siddarth had been expelled with immediate effect in the interest of the party and its movement, adding that he would not be re-inducted in the future.

"In the interest of the party and the movement, Ashok Siddarth has been expelled from the BSP with immediate effect and will not be taken back into the party in future," the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister wrote on X.

Mayawati X post

Explaining the decision, Mayawati noted that Siddarth had earlier been expelled over "indiscipline" during the Maharashtra assembly elections, particularly over issues related to coordination with the party's state unit in ticket distribution.

Mayawati added that Siddharth was subsequently entrusted with organisational responsibilities in states outside Uttar Pradesh to help strengthen the party's base. However, despite repeated warnings, complaints of indiscipline and violation of party directives continued to surface from Karnataka, Odisha and West Bengal, she alleged.

The BSP supremo also clarified that the ex-Rajya Sabha MP had been relieved of all party responsibilities on Saturday.





She further alleged that rumours about his possible return to Uttar Pradesh were being deliberately spread to create confusion within the organisation and derail the BSP's preparations for the next Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

Siddarth, the father-in-law of Mayawati's nephew Akash Anand, was

from the BSP in February last year over alleged "anti-party" activities.

According to Mayawati, Siddharth was re-inducted after he assured the leadership that such lapses would not be repeated.

The BSP chief also announced the expulsion of party coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal on charges of indiscipline and violation of party directives.

According to Mayawati, Beniwal had been entrusted with organisational responsibilities in Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.

World.title: Three die of burns sustained in cylinder blast in Thanjavur district
World.content:
Three persons, who sustained burns in a cooking gas cylinder explosion at Chinna Ammangudi village in Thiruvonam police station limits in Thanjavur district recently, died at the Thanjavur Medical College and Hospital. The police gave the names of the victims as A. Palanivel, 40, V. Kasinathan, 38, and V. Vempaiyan, 45, - all from Chinna Ammangudi.

Ten persons were injured in the blast. A cooking gas cylinder kept inside the thatched shed exploded after the shed caught fire in the early hours on July 30. A few locals who rushed out of their homes to douse the flames sustained burns in the cylinder blast.

The injured were admitted to the Thanjavur Medical College and Hospital. Police sources said Palanivel died of injuries on Saturday evening while Kasinathan and Vempaiyan died on Sunday. The autopsy was conducted on the three bodies and was handed over to their relatives. The Thiruvonam police have registered a case.

World.title: Kerala High Court allows ‘last chance’ to local bodies to clean out illegal flex boards
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has asked the State Chief Secretary to file a statement on the action taken regarding the alleged violations of court directives concerning unauthorised flex hoardings in the State.

The court cautioned the Joint Directors of Urban Affairs and Secretaries of the Local Self-Government Institutions against strict action if violations continued. The Bench remarked that it would be a ‘sheer mockery’ of the court if the authorities vested with jurisdiction over this matter ‘slumbered’ over their duties. It ordered all the Secretaries of the Local Self-Government Institutions to ensure that the territories under them are cleared out and that no further installations are allowed by ‘any class of persons.’

Justice Devan Ramachandran was considering a report by the Amicus Curiae regarding the installation of unauthorised flex boards, banners, posters and flags in public places across various parts of the State.

FIFA World Cup

It was reported that as part of the widespread celebrations of the FIFA World Cup 2026, several unauthorised hoardings, posters and national flags of participating countries were erected in public spaces. These displays were found fastened to pedestrian railings, lamp posts and other public infrastructure using plastic ropes and similar materials. Oversized flex boards were also seen on public land without permission.

In Thiruvananthapuram, boards and flags were observed in a continuous row along the road leading to the Forest Headquarters, Vazhuthacaud, attached to handrails and blocking pedestrian pathways. It was noted that the displays were in connection with an election to a merchants’ association, and that the candidates were the major violators.

Hundreds of flags and flex boards erected by the Forest Protective Staff Association in the Chinnakkada roundabout in Kollam were brought to the court’s notice. The board erected by the Indian Youth Congress in Ponmundam, Malappuram, for the Standing Counsel of the Kerala Pollution Control Board was also reported to the court, and the irony of the violation was not lost on the Bench.

The court stated that it was aware of the protocols issued in Tamil Nadu regarding the unauthorised fixation of flex boards to curb visual pollution.

World.title: Farmers in Kerala’s Thrissur await over ₹10 crore in paddy dues as Onam nears
World.content:
Hundreds of paddy farmers in Thrissur district are anxiously awaiting more than ₹10 crore in pending payments for paddy procured by the Kerala State Civil Supplies Corporation (Supplyco), with uncertainty over the release of funds casting a shadow over the upcoming Onam season.

Farmers said they were yet to receive payment for the Mundakan crop harvested during January and February and the Puncha crop procured during April and May. They alleged that there was no clarity on when the dues would be credited.

According to farmers, more than ₹3 crore remains pending for cultivators in Punnayurkulam, Vadekkad and Punnayur grama panchayats alone. A total of 329 farmers from the three panchayats sold their paddy to Supplyco, but more than half of them are yet to receive payment.

Fund issue

Payments are routed through the State Bank of India (SBI) and Canara Bank. However, SBI officials said payments were being released as and when funds were received from the government, indicating that the delay was due to the non-availability of funds rather than any banking issue.

The delay has caused widespread concern among farmers, many of whom depend on the procurement proceeds to meet cultivation expenses and household needs ahead of the festival season.

Farmers recalled that during the previous procurement season, payments were cleared only in September after prolonged protests. They had even observed Farmers’ Day as a ‘Black Day’ to highlight the issue.

With this year’s dues also remaining unpaid, farmers fear a repeat of the crisis. A meeting of paddy farmers from the Ponnani region has been convened on August 5 to chalk out an agitation demanding the immediate release of the pending payments.

World.title: BCAS gives nod for domestic cargo from Tiruchi airport
World.content:
Domestic cargo movement at the Tiruchi International Airport is poised to take off following clearance granted by the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), an independent department under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

The BCAS clearance has fulfilled the long-pending demand for domestic cargo movement at the non-metro Tiruchi International Airport, which witnesses more overseas flight services than domestic operations. The BCAS had granted the final security vetting approval recently which has cleared the way for domestic cargo operations at Tiruchi airport.

The approval was accorded after sustained coordination by the Airports Authority of India with the relevant authorities to find a workable and secure solution to facilitate domestic cargo movement from Tiruchi airport. “A dedicated area adjacent to the international export cargo terminal has been identified for handling domestic cargo”, said Tiruchi Airport Director Tiruchi G. Gopalakrishnan.

The airport has been handling only overseas cargo which are exported through international carriers operating from here. Perishable goods such as vegetables, flowers, and fruits account for the maximum of overseas export cargo from Tiruchi, which serves as a key gateway for central and southern districts in the State.

Airport authorities said the BCAS clearance for domestic cargo movement would provide local businesses a faster channel to move goods to major domestic hubs without relying on cargo routed through other airports. Tthe move is set to unlock faster cargo connectivity for industry and trade in the region.

The requirement of a domestic cargo facility has long been highlighted by the industry as a necessity and the BCAS clearance has addressed that gap. “The approval reflects the Airport Authority of India’s continued commitment to strengthening regional connectivity and responding to the genuine, long-standing needs of the trade community. Tiruchi is a vital economic hub and enabling domestic cargo movement will give local businesses quicker access to national markets, support trade and add momentum to the region’s economic growth”, Mr. Gopalakrishnan said.

Customs will not be involved in domestic cargo movement.
